# 5.3-5.5 MUST-IMPLEMENT-FROM-SCRATCH (9 Problems)

**How to practice:** write each from memory on a blank file, then test against the edge cases listed. In an interview, state your assumptions out loud, implement the main path, then *say* which edge cases you would handle next — the reasoning about edges is what separates a mid-level from a senior.

These nine are the highest-leverage exercises in this part. Each is small enough to write in 20-30 minutes and deep enough to be a real signal.

---

### 1. DataLoader: per-request batching + caching

**The contract:** many `load(key)` calls in the same tick produce exactly **one** call to the batch function; the same key loaded twice (across ticks, within the request) is fetched once; each promise settles independently.

```ts
type BatchFn<K, V> = (keys: readonly K[]) => PromiseLike<Array<V | Error>>;

export class DataLoader<K, V> {
  #cache = new Map<K, Promise<V>>();
  #queue: K[] = [];
  #pending: Array<{ resolve: (v: V) => void; reject: (e: Error) => void }> = [];
  #scheduled = false;

  constructor(
    private readonly batchFn: BatchFn<K, V>,
    private readonly options: { maxBatchSize?: number; cache?: boolean } = {},
  ) {}

  load(key: K): Promise<V> {
    if (this.options.cache === false) return this.#immediate([key]);
    const hit = this.#cache.get(key);
    if (hit) return hit;
    const p = new Promise<V>((resolve, reject) => {
      this.#queue.push(key);
      this.#pending.push({ resolve, reject });
    });
    p.catch(() => this.#cache.delete(key));    // never cache a failure: a later field can retry
    this.#cache.set(key, p);
    this.#schedule();
    return p;
  }

  loadMany(keys: readonly K[]): Promise<Array<V | Error>> {
    return Promise.all(keys.map((k) => this.load(k).catch((e) => e as Error)));
  }
  // Bypass the cache and the batching queue: one direct round trip, one promise.
  async #immediate(keys: K[]): Promise<V> {
    try {
      const values = await this.batchFn(keys);
      if (values.length !== keys.length || values[0] instanceof Error) {
        throw values[0] ?? new Error('batchFn arity mismatch');
      }
      return values[0] as V;
    } catch (err) {
      throw err instanceof Error ? err : new Error(String(err));
    }
  }
  prime(key: K, value: V): void { this.#cache.set(key, Promise.resolve(value)); }
  clear(key: K): void { this.#cache.delete(key); }
  clearAll(): void { this.#cache.clear(); }

  #schedule(): void {
    if (this.#scheduled) return;
    this.#scheduled = true;
    // A microtask, not setTimeout(0): the whole selection level settles its
    // load() calls before we touch the database.
    queueMicrotask(() => { this.#scheduled = false; void this.#flush(); });
  }

  async #flush(): Promise<void> {
    if (this.#queue.length === 0) return;
    const keys = this.#queue, pending = this.#pending;
    this.#queue = []; this.#pending = [];
    try { await this.#dispatch(keys, pending); }
    catch (err) { for (const p of pending) p.reject(err as Error); }
  }

  async #dispatch(keys: K[], pending: Array<{ resolve: (v: V) => void; reject: (e: Error) => void }>): Promise<void> {
    const size = this.options.maxBatchSize ?? keys.length;
    for (let i = 0; i < keys.length; i += size) {
      const ks = keys.slice(i, i + size);
      const ps = pending.slice(i, i + size);
      let values: Array<V | Error>;
      try { values = await this.batchFn(ks); }
      catch (err) { for (const p of ps) p.reject(err as Error); continue; }
      if (values.length !== ks.length) {
        for (const p of ps) p.reject(new Error(`batchFn returned ${values.length} values for ${ks.length} keys`));
        continue;
      }
      ks.forEach((_, j) =>
        values[j] instanceof Error ? ps[j].reject(values[j] as Error) : ps[j].resolve(values[j] as V));
    }
  }
}

// ---- one loader set per request ----
export function createLoaders(db: Db) {
  return {
    userById: new DataLoader<string, User>((ids) => db.user.findManyByIds([...ids])),
    productBySku: new DataLoader<string, Product>((skus) => db.product.findManyBySkus([...skus]), {
      maxBatchSize: 500,
    }),
  };
}
// SQL behind the batch function — one set-based query, not a loop:
//   SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ANY($1::uuid[]);
```

*Edge cases:* duplicate keys in one batch; a batch function that resolves with the wrong length; a batch function that *throws* (every key in that slice rejects); `maxBatchSize` splitting a tick into several round trips; caching an `Error`; `cache: false`; `loadMany` returning per-key `Error` values (the DataLoader spec's semantics) rather than rejecting; `prime()` for data you already have; a rejected key not poisoning the cache.

*Follow-ups:* why `queueMicrotask` and not `setTimeout(0)`; how to share the cache across requests safely (you cannot, without invalidation — that is a cache, not a loader); how to thread an `AbortSignal` into the batch function.

---

### 2. Relay-style connection paginator with opaque cursors

**The contract:** `first`/`after` and `last`/`before` both work; cursors are opaque, signed, and versioned; a page is exactly `limit + 1` rows fetched so `hasNextPage` is exact rather than guessed.

```ts
import { createHmac, timingSafeEqual } from 'node:crypto';

export interface PageInfo { hasNextPage: boolean; hasPreviousPage: boolean; startCursor: string | null; endCursor: string | null }
export interface Edge<T> { cursor: string; node: T }
export interface ConnectionArgs { first?: number; last?: number; after?: string; before?: string }
export interface Key { createdAt: string; id: string }        // sort key + unique tiebreaker
export class BadCursor extends Error { readonly code = 'BAD_CURSOR' }

const VERSION = 1;
const secret = process.env.CURSOR_SECRET!;

export function encodeCursor(key: Key): string {
  const payload = Buffer.from(JSON.stringify({ v: VERSION, ...key })).toString('base64url');
  const sig = createHmac('sha256', secret).update(payload).digest('base64url').slice(0, 16);
  return `${payload}.${sig}`;
}

export function decodeCursor(cursor: string): Key {
  const dot = cursor.lastIndexOf('.');
  if (dot < 0) throw new BadCursor('malformed cursor');
  const payload = cursor.slice(0, dot);
  const given = Buffer.from(cursor.slice(dot + 1));
  const want = Buffer.from(createHmac('sha256', secret).update(payload).digest('base64url').slice(0, 16));
  if (given.length !== want.length || !timingSafeEqual(given, want)) throw new BadCursor('bad signature');
  const parsed = JSON.parse(Buffer.from(payload, 'base64url').toString()) as { v: number } & Key;
  if (parsed.v !== VERSION) throw new BadCursor('cursor version mismatch');
  return { createdAt: parsed.createdAt, id: parsed.id };
}

// Forward: strictly "older than the cursor". Backward: strictly "newer".
const forward = (after: Key | null) => after ? '(created_at, id) < ($1, $2)' : 'TRUE';
const backward = (before: Key | null) => before ? '(created_at, id) > ($1, $2)' : 'TRUE';

export function buildSql(args: ConnectionArgs): { sql: string; params: unknown[] } {
  const isForward = args.first !== undefined || args.after !== undefined;
  if (args.first !== undefined && args.last !== undefined) throw new Error('first and last are mutually exclusive');
  const where = isForward ? forward(args.after ? decodeCursor(args.after) : null)
                          : backward(args.before ? decodeCursor(args.before) : null);
  const order = isForward ? 'ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC' : 'ORDER BY created_at ASC, id ASC';
  const limit = Math.min(isForward ? args.first ?? 20 : args.last ?? 20, 200);
  return {
    // limit + 1 -> the extra row is the "is there more" signal, no COUNT(*) needed
    sql: `SELECT id, created_at, status, total FROM orders WHERE ${where} ${order} LIMIT $1`,
    params: [limit + 1],
  };
}

export function connectionFromRows<T extends Key>(rows: T[], args: ConnectionArgs) {
  const isForward = args.first !== undefined || args.after !== undefined;
  const limit = Math.min(isForward ? args.first ?? 20 : args.last ?? 20, 200);
  if (limit < 0) throw new RangeError('first/last must be >= 0');
  if (args.first !== undefined && args.last !== undefined) throw new Error('first and last are mutually exclusive');

  let slice = rows;
  if (isForward && args.after) {
    const a = decodeCursor(args.after);
    slice = rows.filter((r) => r.createdAt < a.createdAt || (r.createdAt === a.createdAt && r.id < a.id));
  } else if (!isForward && args.before) {
    const b = decodeCursor(args.before);
    slice = rows.filter((r) => r.createdAt > b.createdAt || (r.createdAt === b.createdAt && r.id > b.id));
  }

  const hasExtra = slice.length > limit;
  const page = hasExtra ? slice.slice(0, limit) : slice;
  const edges = page.map((node) => ({ cursor: encodeCursor({ createdAt: node.createdAt, id: node.id }), node }));
  return {
    edges,
    pageInfo: {
      hasNextPage: isForward ? hasExtra : page.length > 0,
      hasPreviousPage: isForward ? args.after !== undefined : hasExtra,
      startCursor: edges[0]?.cursor ?? null,
      endCursor: edges.at(-1)?.cursor ?? null,
    },
  };
}
// Index requirement: CREATE INDEX ON orders (status, created_at DESC, id DESC);
```

*Edge cases:* `first` and `last` together; `first: 0`; `first: -1`; `after` **and** `before` (a window); a tampered cursor (must be an error, never a silent reset); a cursor from a different sort or a different list (sign the scope into the payload, or store the scope in the cursor); a non-unique sort column (see #4); the `hasPreviousPage` truth table; an empty page (`startCursor: null`); a cursor older than your retention (decide: `400` with a clear code, or a fresh start — never silent).

---

### 3. Idempotency-key middleware (store, TTL, fingerprint, replay)

**The contract:** a client `Idempotency-Key` makes a non-idempotent request safe to retry; the same key + same payload replays the stored response; the same key + a different payload is a hard error; two concurrent in-flight requests with the same key do not both execute.

```ts
import { createHash, randomUUID } from 'node:crypto';
import type { Request, Response, NextFunction } from 'express';

export interface Record_ {
  key: string; fingerprint: string; state: 'in_flight' | 'done';
  status: number; headers: Record<string, string>; body: string; createdAt: number;
}
export interface Store {
  get(key: string): Promise<Record_ | null>;
  putIfAbsent(rec: Record_, ttl: number): Promise<boolean>;   // atomic SET NX
  complete(key: string, rec: Omit<Record_, 'key'>, ttl: number): Promise<void>;
  release(key: string): Promise<void>;                        // on failure, allow a retry
}

// A canonical fingerprint: key order and whitespace must not change the identity.
// `JSON.stringify` alone does NOT do this: it preserves insertion order, so two
// semantically identical bodies with different key order would hash differently
// and the client would get a spurious 409 on a legitimate retry.
function canonicalize(value: unknown): unknown {
  if (Array.isArray(value)) return value.map(canonicalize);        // arrays: order IS significant
  if (value !== null && typeof value === 'object') {
    const out: Record<string, unknown> = {};
    for (const k of Object.keys(value as object).sort()) {
      out[k] = canonicalize((value as Record<string, unknown>)[k]);
    }
    return out;
  }
  return value;
}
export function fingerprint(req: Request): string {
  const canonical = JSON.stringify(canonicalize({
    method: req.method.toUpperCase(),
    path: req.path,
    query: Object.keys(req.query).sort().map((k) => [k, canonicalize(req.query[k])]),
    body: req.body ?? null,
  }));
  return createHash('sha256').update(canonical).digest('hex');
}

export const IDEMPOTENCY_TTL_SECONDS = 24 * 60 * 60;   // >= the client's max retry window

export function idempotency(store: Store, { failClosed = true } = {}) {
  return async (req: Request, res: Response, next: NextFunction) => {
    const key = req.header('Idempotency-Key');
    if (!key || !['POST', 'PUT', 'PATCH', 'DELETE'].includes(req.method)) return next();
    if (key.length > 255) return res.status(400).json({ code: 'INVALID_IDEMPOTENCY_KEY' });

    const fp = fingerprint(req);
    let reserved = false;
    try {
      reserved = await store.putIfAbsent(
        { key, fingerprint: fp, state: 'in_flight', status: 0, headers: {}, body: '', createdAt: Date.now() },
        IDEMPOTENCY_TTL_SECONDS,
      );
    } catch (err) {
      // The store is down. For money, refuse; for cheap reads, continue.
      if (failClosed) return res.status(503).setHeader('Retry-After', '1')
        .json({ code: 'IDEMPOTENCY_UNAVAILABLE' });
      return next();
    }

    if (!reserved) {
      const existing = await store.get(key);
      if (!existing) return next();                                    // expired between the calls
      if (existing.fingerprint !== fp) {
        return res.status(409).json({ code: 'IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED',
          message: 'This idempotency key was used with a different request payload' });
      }
      if (existing.state === 'in_flight') {
        return res.status(409).setHeader('Retry-After', '1').json({ code: 'IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_FLIGHT' });
      }
      res.status(existing.status);
      for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(existing.headers)) res.setHeader(k, v);
      res.setHeader('Idempotency-Replayed', 'true');
      return res.type(existing.headers['content-type'] ?? 'application/json').send(existing.body);
    }

    // Capture the response so a retry can replay it byte-for-byte.
    const chunks: Buffer[] = [];
    const origWrite = res.write.bind(res);
    const origEnd = res.end.bind(res);
    res.write = ((chunk: any, ...rest: any[]) => { chunks.push(Buffer.from(chunk)); return origWrite(chunk, ...rest); }) as any;
    res.end = ((chunk: any, ...rest: any[]) => {
      if (chunk) chunks.push(Buffer.from(chunk));
      const body = Buffer.concat(chunks);
      const headers: Record<string, string> = {};
      for (const h of ['content-type', 'location', 'etag']) {
        const v = res.getHeader(h);
        if (v !== undefined) headers[h] = String(v);
      }
      const record: Omit<Record_, 'key'> = {
        fingerprint: fp, state: 'done', status: res.statusCode, headers, body: body.toString(), createdAt: Date.now(),
      };
      // A 5xx must NOT be cached as the result: the client should be able to retry for real.
      if (res.statusCode < 500) {
        void store.complete(key, record, IDEMPOTENCY_TTL_SECONDS);
      } else {
        void store.release(key);
      }
      return origEnd(chunk, ...rest);
    }) as any;

    res.setHeader('Idempotency-Key', key);
    res.setHeader('X-Request-Id', req.header('X-Request-Id') ?? randomUUID());
    next();
  };
}
```

*Edge cases:* concurrent same-key requests (only the `SET NX` winner executes; the loser gets `409` + `Retry-After`); key reuse with a different body (`409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED` — never return the wrong cached response); **a `5xx` must not be stored**, or the client is permanently locked out of a failure it was entitled to retry; `401`/`409`/`422` responses *should* be stored (they are final answers for that payload) while `5xx` and network errors should not; key expiry between the reserve and the get; a store outage (fail closed for money); key length and charset limits; the key must be scoped per principal or per tenant, or two users can collide on a guessable key; streaming responses cannot be replayed from a buffer.

---

### 4. Cursor-based pagination helper with stable tiebreakers

**The contract:** given an ordered list and a sort, produce a page and a cursor that cannot skip or duplicate rows, even when the sort key has ties and rows are inserted or deleted concurrently.

```ts
export type SortKey = { [K in string]: string | number | null };

/** Build a total order from a (possibly non-unique) sort key plus a unique tiebreaker. */
export function makeComparer<K extends SortKey>(sort: Array<{ field: keyof K; dir: 'asc' | 'desc' }>) {
  const spec = [...sort, { field: 'id' as keyof K, dir: sort[0]?.dir ?? 'desc' }];  // tiebreaker, same direction
  return (a: K, b: K): number => {
    for (const { field, dir } of spec) {
      const av = a[field] ?? null, bv = b[field] ?? null;
      if (av === bv) continue;
      if (av === null) return 1;                       // nulls last, consistently
      if (bv === null) return -1;
      const cmp = av < bv ? -1 : 1;
      return dir === 'asc' ? cmp : -cmp;
    }
    return 0;                                           // identical rows
  };
}

/**
 * Row-wise "strictly after the anchor" predicate for PostgreSQL, matching
 * makeComparer's order exactly. Returns the SQL fragment AND the parameter
 * array, because the fragment alone is useless to a parameterized driver.
 *
 * With sort = [{created_at,'desc'},{id implied 'desc'}] the generated SQL is:
 *   WHERE (
 *     created_at IS NOT DISTINCT FROM $1 AND (created_at < $1 OR created_at IS NULL)
 *  OR (id < $2)
 *   )
 * Every branch reuses the earlier columns' placeholders (same values, same
 * indices) so a single parameter array drives the whole predicate.
 *
 * For an all-ASCENDING (or all-DESCENDING) sort you can use PostgreSQL's native
 * row comparison instead, which is simpler and lets the planner use a composite
 * index:  WHERE (status, created_at, id) < ($1, $2, $3)
 * That form is NOT valid for mixed directions, which is why this expansion exists.
 */
export function tuplePredicate(
  sort: Array<{ field: string; dir: 'asc' | 'desc' }>,
  anchor: Record<string, string | number | null>,
  idColumn = 'id',
  startParam = 1,
): { sql: string; params: Array<string | number | null> } {
  const cols = [...sort.map((s) => s.field), idColumn];
  const dirs = [...sort.map((s) => s.dir), sort[0]?.dir ?? 'desc'];
  const params: Array<string | number | null> = [];
  const placeholders = cols.map((c, i) => {
    const value = anchor[c];
    if (value === undefined) throw new Error(`cursor is missing sort column "${c}"`);
    params.push(value);
    return `$${startParam + i}`;
  });
  // Equality on the prefix columns must be null-safe, hence IS NOT DISTINCT FROM.
  // "Strictly after" in sort order: ASC -> greater value, DESC -> smaller value.
  // Nulls sort LAST in both directions (the makeComparer convention above), so a
  // NULL row compares greater than every value: after a non-NULL anchor we must
  // also accept `col IS NULL`, and after a NULL anchor nothing else qualifies.
  const clauses = cols.map((_, i) => {
    const eq = cols.slice(0, i).map((c, j) => `${c} IS NOT DISTINCT FROM ${placeholders[j]}`);
    const anchorIsNull = anchor[cols[i]] === null;
    const cmp = `${cols[i]} ${dirs[i] === 'asc' ? '>' : '<'} ${placeholders[i]}`;
    const tail = anchorIsNull ? (dirs[i] === 'asc' ? 'FALSE' : `${cols[i]} IS NOT NULL`) : `${cmp} OR ${cols[i]} IS NULL`;
    return [...eq, tail].join(' AND ');
  });
  return { sql: `(${clauses.join('\n   OR ')})`, params };
}

// Usage:
//   const { sql, params } = tuplePredicate(sort, decodeCursor(cursor), 'id', 2);
//   db.query(`SELECT * FROM orders WHERE tenant_id = $1 AND ${sql}
//            ORDER BY status DESC, created_at DESC, id DESC LIMIT $${2 + params.length}`, [tenantId, ...params]);

export interface Page<T> { items: T[]; nextCursor: string | null; prevCursor: string | null; hasMore: boolean }

export function paginate<T extends { id: string } & SortKey>(
  rows: T[],                                       // already ordered by makeComparer's order, limit+1 long
  sort: Array<{ field: keyof T; dir: 'asc' | 'desc' }>,
  limit: number,
  cursor?: string | null,
): Page<T> {
  const compare = makeComparer(sort);
  let slice = rows;
  if (cursor) {
    const anchor = JSON.parse(Buffer.from(cursor, 'base64url').toString()) as T;
    slice = rows.filter((r) => compare(r, anchor) > 0);   // strictly "after the anchor"
  }
  const hasMore = slice.length > limit;
  const items = hasMore ? slice.slice(0, limit) : slice;
  const encode = (row: T) => Buffer.from(JSON.stringify(pickKeys(row, [...sort.map((s) => s.field), 'id'] as (keyof T)[])))
    .toString('base64url');
  return {
    items,
    hasMore,
    nextCursor: items.length > 0 && (hasMore || cursor) ? encode(items.at(-1)!) : null,
    prevCursor: items.length > 0 ? encode(items[0]) : null,
  };
}
function pickKeys<T extends object, K extends keyof T>(o: T, keys: K[]): Pick<T, K> {
  return Object.fromEntries(keys.map((k) => [k, o[k]])) as Pick<T, K>;
}
```

*Edge cases (this is where the interview is won):* **the sort column is not unique** — 100 orders with the same `created_at`, or two products with the same `price`. Without the `id` tiebreaker, a row on the page boundary is either skipped or repeated. This is the single most important thing to say out loud; **the `WHERE` tuple predicate and the `ORDER BY` must list the same columns in the same directions**, or the comparison is wrong even though the query still runs; `null` handling in the ordering (decide nulls-first or nulls-last and apply it identically in the SQL and in memory); a `LIMIT` cap; a descending sort where the tiebreaker must also be descending, or the boundary comparison inverts; the index must match the sort exactly or pagination is O(n) per page; a cursor with a stale sort order (sign the sort into the cursor); the anchor row itself must be excluded with a *strict* comparison (`>` / `<`), not `>=`, or the boundary row repeats forever; `hasMore` from the extra row, not from a `COUNT(*)`; and a `limit` change between page 1 and page 2 is fine, because a cursor is a position, not an offset.

### 5. JSON Merge Patch applier

**The contract:** implement RFC 7396. A patch is a partial JSON document; `null` removes a member, an absent member is untouched, objects merge recursively, **arrays are replaced wholesale**, and applying a patch twice yields the same result (idempotent).

```ts
type Json = null | boolean | number | string | Json[] | { [k: string]: Json };

export function applyMergePatch<T extends Json>(target: T, patch: unknown): T {
  // A patch that is not an object REPLACES the target entirely.
  if (patch === null || typeof patch !== 'object' || Array.isArray(patch)) {
    return patch as T;
  }
  const base: Record<string, Json> =
    target !== null && typeof target === 'object' && !Array.isArray(target) ? { ...(target as object) } : {};

  for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(patch as Record<string, unknown>)) {
    if (value === null) {
      delete base[key];                      // null = remove the member
    } else if (value !== null && typeof value === 'object' && !Array.isArray(value)) {
      base[key] = applyMergePatch(base[key] ?? {}, value);   // recurse; arrays inside are handled at the leaves
    } else {
      base[key] = value as Json;             // scalars AND arrays replace wholesale
    }
  }
  return base as T;
}

// Guard: a patch must be a plain object, with a depth/size limit, and no prototype keys.
export function assertSafePatch(patch: unknown, { maxDepth = 32, maxKeys = 1000 } = {}): void {
  const walk = (v: unknown, depth: number, seen: number): number => {
    if (depth > maxDepth) throw new Error('patch too deep');
    if (v === null || typeof v !== 'object') return seen;
    if (Array.isArray(v)) return v.reduce((n, x) => walk(x, depth + 1, n), seen);
    let n = seen;
    for (const [k, x] of Object.entries(v)) {
      if (k === '__proto__' || k === 'constructor' || k === 'prototype') throw new Error('forbidden key');
      n = walk(x, depth + 1, n + 1);
      if (n > maxKeys) throw new Error('patch too large');
    }
    return n;
  };
  walk(patch, 0, 0);
}
```

**Worked behaviour**
```ts
const original = { a: 'b', c: { d: 'e', f: 'g' }, list: [1, 2, 3], keep: true };

applyMergePatch(original, { a: 'z', c: { f: null } });
// => { a: 'z', c: { d: 'e' }, list: [1, 2, 3], keep: true }

applyMergePatch(original, { list: [9] });
// => { ...original, list: [9] }        arrays REPLACE, they do not merge

applyMergePatch(original, { a: null });
// => { c: {...}, list: [1,2,3], keep: true }   and `a` is GONE

applyMergePatch(original, { a: null, a2: undefined as never });
// undefined is not valid JSON; if it appears, reject the patch rather than storing it

applyMergePatch(original, ['not', 'an', 'object']);
// => ['not','an','object']            a non-object patch replaces the target

applyMergePatch(original, { a: 'x' });
applyMergePatch(original, { a: 'x' });
// idempotent
```

*Edge cases:* **`null` vs absent** — the entire semantic; you cannot set a field to JSON `null` with a merge patch, which is the standard reason to use RFC 6902 instead; **arrays replace**, so `{"tags":["a"]}` deletes `["a","b","c"]`; a non-object patch replaces the target; the target being `null` or an array while the patch is an object (start from `{}`); `__proto__`/`constructor` keys (prototype pollution — merge-patch-based APIs have been exploited through exactly this); depth and key-count limits (a deeply nested patch is a stack-overflow DoS); `undefined` is not valid JSON, so reject rather than store; the patch must be applied to a **copy** of the target, never by mutating a shared object graph (and never a live ORM entity); the media type is `application/merge-patch+json`, and rejecting a wrong `Content-Type` with `415` is part of the contract; and the response `ETag` must be recomputed after the patch.

*Contrast (say this in the interview):* JSON Patch (`application/json-patch+json`, RFC 6902) is an **operation array** with JSON Pointer paths, which can add/remove/replace array elements (`/items/1/quantity`), `move`/`copy`, and — crucially — `{"op":"test",...}` for optimistic concurrency, applied **atomically** (all or nothing). Merge Patch is one partial document with no array element addressing and no `test`. If you need either, use JSON Patch; if you do not, Merge Patch is far easier for clients.

---

### 6. RFC 9457 error factory + a NestJS exception filter

```ts
// ---- the shared package every service imports ----
export interface FieldError { pointer: string; code: string; detail: string }
export interface Problem {
  type: string; title: string; status: number; detail: string;
  instance?: string; code: string; traceId?: string; errors?: FieldError[];
}
const CATALOGUE: Record<number, { type: string; title: string }> = {
  400: { type: 'bad-request',        title: 'Malformed request' },
  401: { type: 'unauthenticated',    title: 'Authentication required' },
  403: { type: 'forbidden',          title: 'Not permitted' },
  404: { type: 'not-found',          title: 'Not found' },
  409: { type: 'conflict',           title: 'Conflict' },
  415: { type: 'unsupported-media',  title: 'Unsupported media type' },
  422: { type: 'validation-failed',  title: 'One or more fields are invalid' },
  429: { type: 'rate-limited',       title: 'Too many requests' },
  500: { type: 'internal',           title: 'Internal server error' },
  503: { type: 'unavailable',        title: 'Service temporarily unavailable' },
};

export function problem(init: {
  status: number; code: string; detail: string; instance?: string;
  traceId?: string; errors?: FieldError[];
}): Problem {
  const { type, title } = CATALOGUE[init.status] ?? CATALOGUE[500];
  const base: Problem = { type: `urn:problem:service:${type}`, title, status: init.status, detail: init.detail, code: init.code };
  // 5xx bodies are information-free: a fixed detail, no errors array, no ids.
  if (init.status >= 500) return { type: base.type, title, status: init.status, detail: 'Something went wrong on our side', code: init.code, traceId: init.traceId };
  return { ...base, instance: init.instance, traceId: init.traceId, errors: init.errors };
}

export function send(res: Response, p: Problem): void {
  res.status(p.status).type('application/problem+json');
  if (p.traceId) res.setHeader('X-Request-Id', p.traceId);
  res.json(p);
}

// ---- domain -> HTTP mapping, in one testable place ----
export class DomainExceptionMapper {
  toHttp(err: unknown): HttpException {
    if (err instanceof OrderNotFoundError)  return new NotFoundException({ code: 'ORDER_NOT_FOUND' });
    if (err instanceof InventoryShortageError) return new UnprocessableEntityException({ code: 'INSUFFICIENT_INVENTORY' });
    if (err instanceof OrderStateError)    return new ConflictException({ code: 'ILLEGAL_STATE_TRANSITION' });
    if (isUniqueViolation(err))            return new ConflictException({ code: 'DUPLICATE_RESOURCE' });
    if (isForeignKeyViolation(err))        return new BadRequestException({ code: 'INVALID_REFERENCE' });
    return new InternalServerErrorException({ code: 'INTERNAL' });
  }
}
```

```ts
// ---- the NestJS global filter ----
@Catch()
export class ProblemDetailsFilter implements ExceptionFilter {
  constructor(private readonly mapper: DomainExceptionMapper, private readonly logger: LoggerService) {}

  catch(exception: unknown, host: ArgumentsHost): void {
    if (host.getType() !== 'http') throw exception;                 // let ws/rpc layers handle it
    const http = host.switchToHttp();
    const req = http.getRequest<Request>();
    const traceId = (req.headers['x-request-id'] as string) ?? randomUUID();

    const httpErr = exception instanceof HttpException ? exception : this.mapper.toHttp(exception);
    const status = httpErr.getStatus();
    const body = httpErr.getResponse() as { code?: string; message?: string | string[] };

    if (status >= 500) this.logger.error({ err: exception, path: req.originalUrl, traceId });
    else this.logger.debug({ code: body?.code, path: req.originalUrl, traceId });   // 4xx is not an error

    const fieldErrors = Array.isArray(body?.message)
      ? body!.message as string[]
      : undefined;

    send(http.getResponse<Response>(), problem({
      status,
      code: body?.code ?? defaultCodeFor(status),
      detail: typeof body?.message === 'string' ? body.message : (fieldErrors ? 'Validation failed' : httpErr.message),
      instance: req.originalUrl,
      traceId,
      errors: fieldErrors?.map((detail, i) => ({ pointer: `/unknown/${i}`, code: 'INVALID', detail })),
    }));
  }
}
```
*Improve in production:* the `pointer` should come from a custom `exceptionFactory` on the `ValidationPipe` that emits `{ pointer, code, detail }` triples rather than flat strings, so the filter does not have to guess. Wire it once in `configureApp()` so tests and production cannot diverge (5.3.11).

*Edge cases:* `HttpException` vs an unknown throwable; a filter that leaks `exception.message` for a 500; a 4xx logged at `error` level (destroys signal); a `host.getType()` other than `'http'` in a hybrid app; a thrown `string` instead of an `Error`; a response that already started (you cannot change the status — log and destroy the connection); a `429` needing `Retry-After`; ensuring the same `traceId` appears in the body, the header, and the log line.

---

### 7. A typed NestJS module: guard + pipe + interceptor + filter, end to end

```ts
// ---------- DTO ----------
export class ListOrdersQueryDto {
  @IsOptional() @IsEnum(OrderStatus) status?: OrderStatus;
  @IsOptional() @Type(() => Number) @IsInt() @Min(1) @Max(100) limit = 20;
  @IsOptional() @Type(() => Number) @IsInt() @Min(0) offset = 0;
  @IsOptional() @IsISO8601() createdAfter?: string;
}

export class CreateOrderDto {
  @IsString() @Length(3, 200) customerName!: string;
  @IsEmail() customerEmail!: string;
  @IsArray() @ArrayMinSize(1) @ArrayMaxSize(50)
  @ValidateNested({ each: true }) @Type(() => OrderItemDto) items!: OrderItemDto[];
}

// ---------- guard ----------
export const ROLES = 'roles';
export const Roles = (...roles: Role[]) => SetMetadata(ROLES, roles);

@Injectable()
export class RolesGuard implements CanActivate {
  constructor(private readonly reflector: Reflector) {}
  canActivate(ctx: ExecutionContext): boolean {
    const required = this.reflector.getAllAndOverride<Role[]>(ROLES, [ctx.getHandler(), ctx.getClass()]) ?? [];
    if (required.length === 0) return true;
    const { user } = ctx.switchToHttp().getRequest<{ user?: AuthUser }>();
    if (!user) throw new UnauthorizedException('Authentication required');
    if (!required.some((r) => user.roles.includes(r))) throw new ForbiddenException('Insufficient role');
    return true;
  }
}

// ---------- interceptor ----------
@Injectable()
export class HttpLoggingInterceptor implements NestInterceptor {
  constructor(private readonly logger: LoggerService) {}
  intercept(ctx: ExecutionContext, next: CallHandler): Observable<unknown> {
    if (ctx.getType() !== 'http') return next.handle();
    const req = ctx.switchToHttp().getRequest<Request>();
    const res = ctx.switchToHttp().getResponse<Response>();
    const traceId = (req.headers['x-request-id'] as string) ?? randomUUID();
    res.setHeader('x-request-id', traceId);
    const started = process.hrtime.bigint();
    return next.handle().pipe(
      tap(() => this.logger.log({ traceId, method: req.method, path: req.originalUrl,
        status: res.statusCode, ms: Number(process.hrtime.bigint() - started) / 1e6 })),
      catchError((err) => { this.logger.error({ traceId, err, path: req.originalUrl }); return throwError(() => err); }),
    );
  }
}

// ---------- service + repository (framework-free) ----------
@Injectable()
export class OrdersService {
  constructor(
    @Inject(ORDER_REPOSITORY) private readonly repo: OrderRepository,
    private readonly payments: PaymentsService,
  ) {}
  list(q: ListOrdersQueryDto, tenantId: string) { return this.repo.list({ ...q, tenantId }); }
  async create(dto: CreateOrderDto, tenantId: string) {
    const total = dto.items.reduce((sum, i) => sum + i.quantity, 0);
    return this.repo.create({ ...dto, tenantId, status: OrderStatus.DRAFT, total });
  }
}

// ---------- controller ----------
@Controller({ path: 'orders', version: '1' })
@UseGuards(RolesGuard)
@UseInterceptors(HttpLoggingInterceptor)
export class OrdersController {
  constructor(private readonly orders: OrdersService) {}

  @Get()
  list(@Query() q: ListOrdersQueryDto, @Req() req: Request) {
    return this.orders.list(q, (req as any).user.tenantId);
  }

  @Post()
  @Roles('customer', 'admin')
  @HttpCode(HttpStatus.CREATED)
  async create(@Body() dto: CreateOrderDto, @Req() req: Request, @Res({ passthrough: true }) res: Response) {
    const order = await this.orders.create(dto, (req as any).user.tenantId);
    res.location(`/v1/orders/${order.id}`);        // 201 + Location, without losing the pipeline
    return order;
  }
}

// ---------- module ----------
@Module({
  controllers: [OrdersController],
  providers: [
    OrdersService,
    RolesGuard, HttpLoggingInterceptor,
    { provide: ORDER_REPOSITORY, useClass: PrismaOrderRepository },
    { provide: PaymentsService, useClass: StripePaymentsService },
  ],
  exports: [OrdersService],
})
export class OrdersModule {}

// ---------- one shared bootstrap, used by main.ts AND the e2e tests ----------
export function configureApp(app: INestApplication): INestApplication {
  app.setGlobalPrefix('v1');
  app.enableVersioning({ type: VersioningType.URI, defaultVersion: '1' });
  app.useGlobalPipes(new ValidationPipe({
    whitelist: true, forbidNonWhitelisted: true, transform: true,
    stopAtFirstError: false,
    exceptionFactory: (errors) => new UnprocessableEntityException({
      code: 'VALIDATION_FAILED',
      message: errors.flatMap((e) => Object.values(e.constraints ?? {}).map((m) => `${e.property}: ${m}`)),
    }),
  }));
  app.useGlobalFilters(new ProblemDetailsFilter(new DomainExceptionMapper(), logger));
  app.useGlobalInterceptors(new HttpLoggingInterceptor(logger));
  return app;
}
```
*Edge cases:* `@Res({ passthrough: true })` or the `Location` header never gets set; `whitelist` without `forbidNonWhitelisted` (silent drops); a global pipe in `main.ts` only, so e2e tests validate nothing (5.3.11); `@UseInterceptors` on a handler that uses `@Res()` without passthrough (the interceptor never sees it); a role check on the class plus a method-level `@Roles` (method metadata must override, not merge, or a `@Roles('admin')` endpoint also requires `customer`); `errorPolicy` of your validator not reporting all fields; and the 4xx log level.

---

### 8. Webhook signature verifier with timestamp tolerance and constant-time compare

```ts
import { createHmac, timingSafeEqual } from 'node:crypto';

export interface VerifyOptions {
  rawBody: Buffer;              // the EXACT bytes received, before any JSON parsing
  header: string | undefined;   // e.g. "t=1714560000,v1=6f8a...,v1=9c2b..."  (one per active secret)
  secret: string;               // or string[] during rotation
  toleranceSeconds?: number;
  now?: number;
}
export type VerifyResult =
  | { ok: true; timestamp: number }
  | { ok: false; reason: 'missing' | 'malformed' | 'stale' | 'no-matching-secret' | 'bad-signature' };

export function verifyWebhook(o: VerifyOptions): VerifyResult {
  const tolerance = o.toleranceSeconds ?? 300;                    // 5 minutes
  if (!o.header) return { ok: false, reason: 'missing' };
  if (o.rawBody.length === 0) return { ok: false, reason: 'malformed' };
  if (o.rawBody.length > 5 * 1024 * 1024) return { ok: false, reason: 'malformed' };

  // 1. Parse the header into timestamp + the list of candidate signatures.
  const ts: number[] = [], sigs: string[] = [];
  for (const part of o.header.split(',')) {
    const idx = part.indexOf('=');
    if (idx < 0) continue;
    const k = part.slice(0, idx).trim(), v = part.slice(idx + 1).trim();
    if (k === 't') ts.push(Number(v));
    if (k === 'v1' && /^[0-9a-f]{64}$/i.test(v)) sigs.push(v.toLowerCase());   // hex HMAC only
  }
  const timestamp = ts[0];
  if (!Number.isFinite(timestamp) || sigs.length === 0) return { ok: false, reason: 'malformed' };

  // 2. Replay window. Compare absolute skew so a future-dated timestamp is rejected too.
  const skew = Math.abs((o.now ?? Date.now()) / 1000 - timestamp);
  if (skew > tolerance) return { ok: false, reason: 'stale' };

  // 3. Sign timestamp + "." + raw body. The timestamp inside the signed material is what
  //    stops a captured (body, signature) pair from being replayed with a fresh t=.
  const secrets = Array.isArray(o.secret) ? o.secret : [o.secret];
  let matched = false;
  for (const secret of secrets) {
    const expected = createHmac('sha256', secret).update(`${timestamp}.`).update(o.rawBody).digest();
    for (const sig of sigs) {
      const given = Buffer.from(sig, 'hex');
      // length check first: timingSafeEqual throws on a length mismatch.
      if (given.length === expected.length && timingSafeEqual(given, expected)) { matched = true; break; }
    }
    if (matched) break;
  }
  return matched ? { ok: true, timestamp } : { ok: false, reason: 'bad-signature' };
}

// Raw-body capture you need for the verifier to work at all:
app.post('/webhooks/stripe',
  express.raw({ type: 'application/json' }),                 // Buffer, not an object
  (req, res) => {
    const verdict = verifyWebhook({ rawBody: req.body, header: req.header('stripe-signature'),
                                    secret: process.env.STRIPE_SECRET! });
    if (!verdict.ok) return res.status(400).type('application/problem+json')
      .json({ type: 'bad-signature', title: 'Bad request', status: 400, code: 'INVALID_SIGNATURE' });
    const event = JSON.parse(req.body.toString());
    // Atomic dedupe: the insert's conflict result IS the idempotency check.
    void enqueue(event).catch((err) => res.status(500).end());
    res.status(200).end();                                     // fast 2xx, process async
  });
```
*Edge cases:* **verifying after re-serializing the parsed body** (the signature will not match — this is the classic bug); signing the body without the timestamp (replayable forever); naive `===` (byte-by-byte timing leak); `timingSafeEqual` throwing on a length mismatch; **secret rotation** (emit one `v1=` per active secret and accept any — hence `string[]`); a header with several `v1=` values for the same secret; a non-hex or wrong-length signature; a timestamp in seconds vs milliseconds; a clock skew that rejects valid deliveries (the tolerance, and the receiver's NTP requirement); a signature replayed within the tolerance window (the tolerance is the mitigation — hence also dedupe on `id`); multiple headers with the same name; `t=` present but no `v1=`; and a very large body (cap it before hashing, or a single request can make you hash 100 MB).

---

### 9. GraphQL query depth and complexity validator

```ts
type FieldInfo = { name: string; type: TypeInfo; args: Record<string, unknown> };
type TypeInfo = { kind: 'scalar' | 'object' | 'union' | 'interface' | 'enum'; name: string; ofType?: TypeInfo };
interface TypeMap { [name: string]: { fields: Record<string, FieldInfo>; listSizeHint?: number } }

export interface Limits { maxDepth: number; maxCost: number; maxAliases: number; maxRootFields: number }
export type Verdict = { ok: true; cost: number; depth: number } | { ok: false; code: string; message: string; cost?: number };

export function validateQuery(schema: TypeMap, rootType: string, doc: any, limits: Limits): Verdict {
  let cost = 0, depth = 0, aliases = 0, rootFields = 0;
  const fragments = new Map<string, any>(
    (doc.definitions ?? []).filter((d: any) => d.kind === 'FragmentDefinition').map((d: any) => [d.name.value, d]),
  );

  // 1. Depth + cost in one pass. Fragment spreads are expanded with cycle detection.
  const walk = (selections: any[], parentType: string, level: number, visiting: Set<string>): void => {
    if (level > limits.maxDepth) {
      throw Object.assign(new Error('depth limit exceeded'), { code: 'DEPTH_LIMIT' });
    }
    for (const sel of selections ?? []) {
      if (sel.kind === 'Field') {
        aliases += 1;
        const name = sel.name.value;
        const typeInfo = schema[parentType]?.fields?.[name]?.type;
        if (!typeInfo) continue;
        // List fields multiply the cost of everything beneath them. The multiplier is
        // the *effective* page size: the client's `first`, capped by the schema hint.
        const requested = Number((sel.arguments ?? []).find((a: any) => a.name.value === 'first')?.value?.value ?? 0);
        const listSize = typeInfo.kind === 'object' && isList(typeInfo)
          ? Math.min(requested || schema[unwrapped(typeInfo)]?.listSizeHint ?? 10, 200)
          : 1;
        const fieldCost = 1 * listSize;
        cost += fieldCost;
        if (typeInfo.kind === 'object') {
          walk(sel.selectionSet?.selections ?? [], unwrapped(typeInfo).name, level + 1, visiting);
        } else if (typeInfo.kind === 'union' || typeInfo.kind === 'interface') {
          // Only inline fragments can select further fields; charge the widest branch.
          const branches = (sel.selectionSet?.selections ?? []).filter((s: any) => s.kind === 'InlineFragment');
          for (const b of branches) walk(b.selectionSet?.selections ?? [], b.typeCondition?.name?.value ?? parentType, level + 1, visiting);
        }
      } else if (sel.kind === 'InlineFragment') {
        walk(sel.selectionSet?.selections ?? [], sel.typeCondition?.name?.value ?? parentType, level, visiting);
      } else if (sel.kind === 'FragmentSpread') {
        const name = sel.name.value;
        if (visiting.has(name)) {
          throw Object.assign(new Error('fragment cycle'), { code: 'FRAGMENT_CYCLE' });
        }
        const frag = fragments.get(name);
        if (!frag) throw Object.assign(new Error('unknown fragment'), { code: 'UNKNOWN_FRAGMENT' });
        visiting.add(name);
        walk(frag.selectionSet?.selections, frag.typeCondition?.name?.value ?? parentType, level, visiting);
        visiting.delete(name);
      }
    }
  };

  try {
    for (const def of doc.definitions ?? []) {
      if (def.kind !== 'OperationDefinition') continue;
      rootFields += def.selectionSet?.selections?.length ?? 0;
      walk(def.selectionSet?.selections, rootType, 1, new Set());
    }
  } catch (err: any) {
    return { ok: false, code: err.code ?? 'VALIDATION_FAILED', message: err.message };
  }

  if (aliases > limits.maxAliases)     return { ok: false, code: 'ALIAS_LIMIT',   message: `max ${limits.maxAliases} fields per query` };
  if (rootFields > limits.maxRootFields) return { ok: false, code: 'ROOT_LIMIT',  message: `max ${limits.maxRootFields} root fields` };
  if (cost > limits.maxCost)           return { ok: false, code: 'COMPLEXITY_LIMIT', message: `estimated cost ${cost} > ${limits.maxCost}`, cost };
  return { ok: true, cost, depth };
}

const isList = (t: TypeInfo) => t.kind === 'object' && !!t.ofType;
const unwrapped = (t: TypeInfo): TypeInfo => (t.ofType ? unwrapped(t.ofType) : t);
```

*Edge cases:* **list amplification** — a nested list field multiplies, so `orders(first: 1000) { items(first: 1000) { variants { price } } }` must be priced at 10^6, not counted as 4 fields; a field count limit alone is trivially bypassed (debugging/interview favourite); `first: 1000` vs a schema cap of 100 — price what you will actually serve, and clamp the argument *before* it reaches the resolver; **fragment cycles** (`fragment A on T { ...B } fragment B on T { ...A }`) cause infinite recursion and a stack overflow, so track the visiting set; **unknown fragments**; unions and interfaces (only inline fragments select further fields, and the branches are alternatives, not cumulative — charging the sum over-counts, charging the max under-counts for authorization, so be deliberate); a cost of 0 for a query that only has introspection fields (and remember introspection is off in production anyway); the estimation happening **before execution**, so a rejection costs nothing; a hard server-side timeout as a second line of defence for a query that under-estimates; and combining this with a per-operation token bucket so a *repeated* expensive query is throttled by cost rather than rejected every time.
