## Problem 2 — Rate limiter: token bucket, sliding window, and an atomic distributed script

**Difficulty:** 🔴 Advanced · **Must-know**

**Requirement.** Three policies behind one interface, O(1) per call, idle-key eviction, plus the atomic Redis contract.

```ts
// ───────────────────────── rate-limiter.ts ─────────────────────────
export interface Decision { allowed: boolean; limit: number; remaining: number; retryAfterMs: number; resetAt?: number; policy: string; }
export interface RateLimiter { tryAcquire(key: string, cost?: number): Promise<Decision>; }

export class TokenBucketLimiter implements RateLimiter {
  private readonly buckets = new Map<string, { tokens: number; last: number; seen: number }>();
  constructor(private readonly capacity: number, private readonly refillPerSec: number,
              private readonly opts: { idleMs?: number; clock?: () => number } = {}) {
    if (capacity < 1 || refillPerSec <= 0) throw new RangeError('invalid bucket config');
  }
  async tryAcquire(key: string, cost = 1): Promise<Decision> {
    const now = (this.opts.clock ?? Date.now)();
    if (cost > this.capacity)
      return { allowed: false, limit: this.capacity, remaining: 0, retryAfterMs: Infinity, policy: 'token-bucket' };
    const b = this.buckets.get(key) ?? { tokens: this.capacity, last: now, seen: now };
    const tokens = Math.min(this.capacity, b.tokens + ((now - b.last) / 1000) * this.refillPerSec);
    b.last = now; b.seen = now;
    if (tokens < cost) {
      b.tokens = tokens; this.buckets.set(key, b);
      const waitMs = Math.ceil(((cost - tokens) / this.refillPerSec) * 1000);
      return { allowed: false, limit: this.capacity, remaining: Math.floor(tokens), retryAfterMs: waitMs,
               resetAt: now + waitMs, policy: 'token-bucket' };
    }
    b.tokens = tokens - cost; this.buckets.set(key, b);
    return { allowed: true, limit: this.capacity, remaining: Math.floor(b.tokens), retryAfterMs: 0,
             resetAt: now + Math.ceil(((this.capacity - b.tokens) / this.refillPerSec) * 1000), policy: 'token-bucket' };
  }
  /** Prevents unbounded growth — mandatory in production. */
  sweep(now = (this.opts.clock ?? Date.now)()): void {
    const idle = this.opts.idleMs ?? 600_000;
    for (const [k, b] of this.buckets) if (now - b.seen > idle) this.buckets.delete(k);
  }
}

export class SlidingWindowCounterLimiter implements RateLimiter {
  private readonly state = new Map<string, { win: number; cur: number; prev: number; seen: number }>();
  constructor(private readonly windowMs: number, private readonly limitPerWindow: number,
              private readonly opts: { clock?: () => number } = {}) {
    if (windowMs < 1) throw new RangeError('invalid window');
  }
  async tryAcquire(key: string, cost = 1): Promise<Decision> {
    const now = (this.opts.clock ?? Date.now)();
    const w = Math.floor(now / this.windowMs);
    const s = this.state.get(key) ?? { win: w, cur: 0, prev: 0, seen: now };
    if (s.win !== w) {                                          // rotate, carrying the weighted previous count
      const elapsed = now - w * this.windowMs;
      s.prev = elapsed === 0 ? s.cur : Math.ceil(s.cur * (1 - elapsed / this.windowMs));
      s.cur = 0; s.win = w;
    }
    s.seen = now;
    const position = (now - w * this.windowMs) / this.windowMs;   // 0..1
    const estimate = s.prev * (1 - position) + s.cur;
    this.state.set(key, s);
    if (estimate + cost > this.limitPerWindow) {
      const retryAfterMs = Math.ceil((1 - position) * this.windowMs);
      return { allowed: false, limit: this.limitPerWindow, remaining: 0, retryAfterMs,
               resetAt: now + retryAfterMs, policy: 'sliding-window-counter' };
    }
    s.cur += cost;
    return { allowed: true, limit: this.limitPerWindow,
             remaining: Math.max(0, Math.floor(this.limitPerWindow - estimate - cost)), retryAfterMs: 0,
             resetAt: (w + 1) * this.windowMs, policy: 'sliding-window-counter' };
  }
  sweep(now = (this.opts.clock ?? Date.now)()): void {
    for (const [k, s] of this.state) if (now - s.seen > 2 * this.windowMs) this.state.delete(k);
  }
}

/**
 * THE DISTRIBUTED CONTRACT. A read-then-write in a shared store races: N concurrent requests all
 * observe "count = limit-1" and all pass. The fix is ONE atomic operation — in Redis a Lua script.
 * This is the single most important implementation detail of the whole problem.
 */
export const SLIDING_WINDOW_LUA = `
local key, now, window, limit, cost = KEYS[1], tonumber(ARGV[1]), tonumber(ARGV[2]), tonumber(ARGV[3]), tonumber(ARGV[4])
redis.call('ZREMRANGEBYSCORE', key, '-inf', now - window)
local used = redis.call('ZCARD', key)
if used + cost > limit then
  local oldest = redis.call('ZRANGE', key, 0, 0, 'WITHSCORES')
  return {0, limit - used, tonumber(oldest[2]) + window - now}
end
for i = 1, cost do redis.call('ZADD', key, now, now .. '-' .. i .. '-' .. math.random()) end
redis.call('PEXPIRE', key, window)
return {1, limit - used - cost, 0}
`;

/** Concurrency limiter: caps IN-FLIGHT work, not rate. Often the right answer for expensive work. */
export class ConcurrencyLimiter {
  private available: number; private readonly waiters: (() => void)[] = [];
  constructor(private readonly capacity: number, private readonly queueLimit = 0) {
    if (capacity < 1) throw new RangeError('capacity must be >= 1');
    this.available = capacity;
  }
  async acquire(): Promise<() => void> {
    if (this.available > 0) { this.available--; return this.release(); }
    if (this.queueLimit === 0) throw new BulkheadFull('no queue: fail fast');
    if (this.waiters.length >= this.queueLimit) throw new BulkheadFull('queue full');
    return new Promise(res => this.waiters.push(() => { this.available--; res(this.release()); }));
  }
  private release(): () => void {
    let done = false;
    return () => { if (done) return; done = true; this.available++; const n = this.waiters.shift(); if (n) n(); };
  }
}
export class BulkheadFull extends Error {}
```

```ts
// ───────────────────────── rate-limiter.test.ts ─────────────────────────
import { TokenBucketLimiter, SlidingWindowCounterLimiter, ConcurrencyLimiter, BulkheadFull } from './rate-limiter';
let now = 0; const clock = () => now;
const test = (name: string, fn: () => void | Promise<void>) =>
  Promise.resolve().then(fn).then(() => console.log('  ok', name),
    e => { console.error('  FAIL', name, (e as Error).message); process.exitCode = 1; });

await test('token bucket: burst then refill', async () => {
  const rl = new TokenBucketLimiter(3, 1, { clock });
  const r = [await rl.tryAcquire('u1'), await rl.tryAcquire('u1'), await rl.tryAcquire('u1'), await rl.tryAcquire('u1')];
  if (!r[0]!.allowed || !r[2]!.allowed) throw new Error('first 3 should pass');
  if (r[3]!.allowed) throw new Error('4th should be blocked');
  if (r[3]!.retryAfterMs !== 1000) throw new Error(`retryAfter should be 1000, got ${r[3]!.retryAfterMs}`);
  now += 1000;
  if (!(await rl.tryAcquire('u1')).allowed) throw new Error('should refill after 1s');
});
await test('token bucket never exceeds capacity no matter how long you wait', async () => {
  const rl = new TokenBucketLimiter(2, 100, { clock });
  now += 10_000;
  let allowed = 0; for (let i = 0; i < 5; i++) if ((await rl.tryAcquire('u1')).allowed) allowed++;
  if (allowed !== 2) throw new Error(`expected 2, got ${allowed}`);
});
await test('sliding window: no boundary double-burst', async () => {
  const rl = new SlidingWindowCounterLimiter(1000, 5, { clock });
  now = 999;
  let a = 0; for (let i = 0; i < 5; i++) if ((await rl.tryAcquire('u')).allowed) a++;
  now = 1000;
  let b = 0; for (let i = 0; i < 5; i++) if ((await rl.tryAcquire('u')).allowed) b++;
  if (a !== 5) throw new Error('first window should allow 5');
  if (b >= 5) throw new Error(`boundary burst leaked: ${b} allowed immediately after`);
});
await test('keys are independent', async () => {
  const rl = new TokenBucketLimiter(1, 1, { clock });
  if (!(await rl.tryAcquire('a')).allowed) throw new Error('a should pass');
  if ((await rl.tryAcquire('a')).allowed) throw new Error('a should be blocked');
  if (!(await rl.tryAcquire('b')).allowed) throw new Error('b has its own bucket');
});
await test('idle keys are swept', async () => {
  const rl = new TokenBucketLimiter(5, 1, { clock, idleMs: 1000 });
  await rl.tryAcquire('x'); now += 2000; rl.sweep();
  if (!(await rl.tryAcquire('x')).allowed) throw new Error('a fresh key should get a full bucket');
});
await test('concurrency limiter fails fast when saturated', async () => {
  const cl = new ConcurrencyLimiter(1, 0);
  const release = await cl.acquire();
  try { await cl.acquire(); throw new Error('should have thrown BulkheadFull'); }
  catch (e) { if (!(e instanceof BulkheadFull)) throw e; }
  release();
  await cl.acquire();
});
console.log('rate-limiter tests done');
```

**Follow-ups.** Fail open vs closed (public abuse protection fails open or falls back to a local limiter; billing fails closed — say which and add a metric). Hierarchical limits (per-user *and* per-tenant *and* global). Where to run it: at the edge to reject before consuming app capacity, plus a local defence in depth. Rate vs concurrency vs quota.

## Problem 3 — Typed event emitter with isolation, unsubscribe, and async fan-out

**Difficulty:** 🟢 Beginner · **Must-know**

**Requirement.** `on` returns an unsubscribe function; duplicate subscriptions impossible; dispatch isolated so one throwing listener cannot stop the rest; safe under concurrent modification; async fan-out modes.

```ts
// ─────────────────────────── emitter.ts ───────────────────────────
export type Listener<T> = (payload: T) => void | Promise<void>;
export class TooManyListeners extends Error { constructor(evt: string, n: number, max: number) {
  super(`${n} listeners on "${evt}" (max ${max}) — likely a leak`); } }
export class AggregateDispatchError extends Error {
  constructor(evt: string, readonly errs: unknown[]) { super(`${errs.length} listener(s) failed for "${evt}"`, { cause: errs[0] }); } }

export class Emitter<Events extends Record<string, unknown>> {
  private readonly listeners = new Map<keyof Events, Set<Listener<never>>>();
  private readonly onError?: (evt: string, err: unknown, idx: number) => void;
  constructor(private readonly opts: { maxListeners?: number; onError?: (evt: string, err: unknown, idx: number) => void } = {}) {
    this.opts.maxListeners && 0;
  }
  private get maxListeners() { return this.opts.maxListeners ?? 50; }

  on<K extends keyof Events>(evt: K, fn: Listener<Events[K]>): () => void {
    let set = this.listeners.get(evt);
    if (!set) this.listeners.set(evt, (set = new Set()));
    if (set.size >= this.maxListeners) throw new TooManyListeners(String(evt), set.size, this.maxListeners);
    set.add(fn as Listener<never>);
    return () => this.off(evt, fn);                       // the disposer is part of the API
  }
  once<K extends keyof Events>(evt: K, fn: Listener<Events[K]>): () => void {
    const off = this.on(evt, async p => { off(); await fn(p); });
    return off;
  }
  off<K extends keyof Events>(evt: K, fn: Listener<Events[K]>) { this.listeners.get(evt)?.delete(fn as Listener<never>); }
  listenerCount<K extends keyof Events>(evt: K) { return this.listeners.get(evt)?.size ?? 0; }
  eventNames() { return [...this.listeners.keys()]; }

  /** Sync, isolated, snapshot-iterated. */
  emit<K extends keyof Events>(evt: K, payload: Events[K]): void {
    const snapshot = [...(this.listeners.get(evt) ?? [])];     // copy: a listener may mutate the set
    snapshot.forEach((fn, i) => {
      try { const r = fn(payload); if (r instanceof Promise) r.catch(e => this.opts.onError?.(String(evt), e, i)); }
      catch (e) { this.opts.onError?.(String(evt), e, i); }     // isolate: continue
    });
  }
  /** Deterministic start order, concurrent execution, aggregated failures. */
  async emitAsync<K extends keyof Events>(evt: K, payload: Events[K], mode: 'parallel' | 'sequential' = 'parallel'): Promise<void> {
    const snapshot = [...(this.listeners.get(evt) ?? [])] as Listener<Events[K]>[];
    const failures: unknown[] = [];
    if (mode === 'sequential') {
      for (const fn of snapshot) { try { await fn(payload); } catch (e) { failures.push(e); } }
    } else {
      const settled = await Promise.allSettled(snapshot.map(fn => fn(payload)));
      for (const r of settled) if (r.status === 'rejected') failures.push(r.reason);
    }
    failures.forEach((e, i) => this.opts.onError?.(String(evt), e, i));
    if (failures.length) throw new AggregateDispatchError(String(evt), failures);
  }
}
```

```ts
// ─────────────────────────── emitter.test.ts ───────────────────────────
import { Emitter, AggregateDispatchError } from './emitter';
type Ev = { ping: { n: number } };
const test = (name: string, fn: () => void | Promise<void>) =>
  Promise.resolve().then(fn).then(() => console.log('  ok', name),
    e => { console.error('  FAIL', name, (e as Error).message); process.exitCode = 1; });

await test('unsubscribe removes the listener', () => {
  const e = new Emitter<Ev>(); const seen: number[] = [];
  const off = e.on('ping', p => { seen.push(p.n); });
  e.emit('ping', { n: 1 }); off(); e.emit('ping', { n: 2 });
  if (seen.length !== 1) throw new Error('should have been removed');
});
await test('duplicate subscription is impossible (Set semantics)', () => {
  const e = new Emitter<Ev>(); let calls = 0; const fn = () => { calls++; };
  e.on('ping', fn); e.on('ping', fn); e.emit('ping', { n: 1 });
  if (calls !== 1) throw new Error(`called ${calls} times`);
});
await test('a throwing listener does not stop the others', () => {
  const errors: unknown[] = [];
  const e = new Emitter<Ev>({ onError: (_e, err) => errors.push(err) });
  const seen: string[] = [];
  e.on('ping', () => { throw new Error('A fails'); });
  e.on('ping', () => { seen.push('B'); });
  e.on('ping', () => { seen.push('C'); });
  e.emit('ping', { n: 1 });
  if (seen.join(',') !== 'B,C') throw new Error(`others must run: ${seen}`);
  if (errors.length !== 1) throw new Error('error should be reported');
});
await test('a listener may unsubscribe during dispatch without skipping others', () => {
  const e = new Emitter<Ev>(); const seen: string[] = [];
  const offB = e.on('ping', () => { seen.push('B'); offB(); });
  e.on('ping', () => { seen.push('C'); }); e.on('ping', () => { seen.push('D'); });
  e.emit('ping', { n: 1 });
  if (seen.join(',') !== 'B,C,D') throw new Error(`got ${seen}`);
});
await test('emitAsync aggregates all failures', async () => {
  const e = new Emitter<Ev>({ onError: () => {} });
  e.on('ping', async () => { throw new Error('x'); });
  e.on('ping', async () => {});
  e.on('ping', async () => { throw new Error('y'); });
  try { await e.emitAsync('ping', { n: 1 }); throw new Error('should have thrown'); }
  catch (err) { if (!(err instanceof AggregateDispatchError) || err.errs.length !== 2) throw err; }
});
await test('an async listener rejection in emit() is caught, not unhandled', async () => {
  let reported = 0;
  const e = new Emitter<Ev>({ onError: () => { reported++; } });
  e.on('ping', async () => { throw new Error('async boom'); });
  e.emit('ping', { n: 1 });
  await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 10));
  if (reported !== 1) throw new Error('async rejection must be reported');
});
await test('the listener limit fires (leak detector)', () => {
  const e = new Emitter<Ev>({ maxListeners: 2 });
  e.on('ping', () => {}); e.on('ping', () => {});
  try { e.on('ping', () => {}); throw new Error('should have thrown'); }
  catch (err) { if (!(err instanceof Error) || !err.message.includes('leak')) throw err; }
});
console.log('emitter tests done');
```

**Follow-ups.** Backpressure (streams with `bufferSize`, or a queue). When to move to a broker (independent deploy/scale, or replay). Testing (inject the emitter, subscribe a spy, assert call + payload; assert the disposer works; never assert ordering unless you chose `sequential`). `maxListeners` as a design signal.

## Problem 4 — Parking lot with strategies, atomic allocation, and fees

**Difficulty:** 🔴 Advanced · **Must-know**

**Requirement.** Multi-floor lot with sized slots; `park`, `unpark` (with fees), `findFreeSlots`, `findVehiclesByColor`, `findSlotsBySize`; swappable allocation and pricing strategies; atomic entry.

```ts
// ─────────────────────────── parking.ts ───────────────────────────
export type VehicleType = 'motorbike' | 'compact' | 'large';
export type SlotSize = 'motorbike' | 'compact' | 'large';
export type Color = 'red' | 'blue' | 'green' | 'white' | 'black' | 'yellow';
export interface SlotRef { floor: number; row: number; number: number; }
const reqSize: Record<VehicleType, SlotSize> = { motorbike: 'motorbike', compact: 'compact', large: 'large' };
const SIZE_ORDER: SlotSize[] = ['motorbike', 'compact', 'large'];

export class Vehicle {
  private constructor(readonly plate: string, readonly type: VehicleType, readonly color: Color) {}
  static of(plate: string, type: VehicleType, color: Color): Vehicle {
    const p = plate.trim().toUpperCase();
    if (!/^[A-Z0-9]{3,10}$/.test(p)) throw new InvalidPlate(plate);
    return new Vehicle(p, type, color);
  }
}
export class Slot {
  private occupant: Vehicle | null = null;
  constructor(readonly ref: SlotRef, readonly size: SlotSize, readonly accessible = false, readonly evCharging = false) {}
  get isFree() { return this.occupant === null; }
  get current() { return this.occupant; }
  fits(v: Vehicle) { return SIZE_ORDER.indexOf(this.size) >= SIZE_ORDER.indexOf(reqSize[v.type]); }
  /** THE ATOMIC CHECK-AND-SET. This is what makes concurrent park() safe. */
  occupy(v: Vehicle): void {
    if (this.occupant) throw new SlotOccupied(this.ref);
    if (!this.fits(v)) throw new VehicleTooLarge(v.type, this.size);
    this.occupant = v;
  }
  vacate(): Vehicle {
    const v = this.occupant; if (!v) throw new SlotAlreadyFree(this.ref);
    this.occupant = null; return v;
  }
}
export class Floor {
  readonly slots: Slot[] = [];
  private readonly freeBySize = new Map<SlotSize, Set<Slot>>();
  constructor(readonly id: number, readonly rows: number, readonly slotsPerRow: number,
              private readonly zoning: (ref: SlotRef) => SlotSize = defaultZoning,
              opts: { accessibleEvery?: number; evEvery?: number } = {}) {
    const acc = opts.accessibleEvery ?? 0, ev = opts.evEvery ?? 0;
    for (let r = 1; r <= rows; r++) for (let s = 1; s <= slotsPerRow; s++) {
      const ref: SlotRef = { floor: id, row: r, number: s };
      const slot = new Slot(ref, zoning(ref), acc > 0 && s % acc === 0, ev > 0 && s % ev === 0);
      this.slots.push(slot); this.indexFree(slot);
    }
  }
  indexFree(s: Slot) { let set = this.freeBySize.get(s.size); if (!set) this.freeBySize.set(s.size, (set = new Set())); set.add(s); }
  unindexFree(s: Slot) { this.freeBySize.get(s.size)?.delete(s); }
  freeSlots(size: SlotSize) { return this.freeBySize.get(size) ?? new Set<Slot>(); }
  freeCountBySize() { return new Map(SIZE_ORDER.map(s => [s, this.freeSlots(s).size] as [SlotSize, number])); }
  slotAt(ref: SlotRef): Slot {
    const s = this.slots.find(x => x.row === ref.row && x.number === ref.number);
    if (!s) throw new NoSuchSlot(ref); return s;
  }
}
export function defaultZoning(ref: SlotRef): SlotSize {
  return ref.number <= 6 ? 'motorbike' : ref.number <= 14 ? 'compact' : 'large';
}

// ── Strategies ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
export interface SlotAllocator { readonly name: string; allocate(c: readonly Slot[], v: Vehicle): Slot; }
export const FirstFit: SlotAllocator = { name: 'first-fit',
  allocate: (c, v) => { const s = c.find(x => x.isFree && x.fits(v)); if (!s) throw new NoSlotAvailable(v.type); return s; } };
export const NearestToEntrance: SlotAllocator = { name: 'nearest',
  allocate: (c, v) => { const s = c.filter(x => x.isFree && x.fits(v)).sort((a, b) => a.ref.number - b.ref.number)[0];
                       if (!s) throw new NoSlotAvailable(v.type); return s; } };
export const AccessibleOnly: SlotAllocator = { name: 'accessible-only',
  allocate: (c, v) => { const s = c.find(x => x.isFree && x.fits(v) && x.accessible); if (!s) throw new NoSlotAccessible(v.type); return s; } };
export const EvOnly: SlotAllocator = { name: 'ev-only',
  allocate: (c, v) => { const s = c.find(x => x.isFree && x.fits(v) && x.evCharging); if (!s) throw new NoSlotEv(v.type); return s; } };

export interface RateStrategy { feeFor(hours: number): number; }   // minor units (cents)
export const HOURLY: Record<VehicleType, RateStrategy> = {
  motorbike: { feeFor: h => h * 100 }, compact: { feeFor: h => h * 300 }, large: { feeFor: h => h * 500 } };

export class Ticket { constructor(readonly id: string, readonly slot: SlotRef, readonly issuedAt: number) {} }
export interface TxRunner { run<T>(fn: () => Promise<T> | T): Promise<T>; }
export const NoTransaction: TxRunner = { run: fn => Promise.resolve(fn()) };

export class ParkingLot {
  private readonly byTicket = new Map<string, { ticket: Ticket; vehicle: Vehicle }>();
  private readonly byColor = new Map<Color, Set<Slot>>();
  private ticketSeq = 0;
  constructor(private readonly floors: Floor[], private readonly allocators: ReadonlyMap<number, SlotAllocator>,
              private readonly rates: Record<VehicleType, RateStrategy>, private readonly clock: { now(): number },
              private readonly tx: TxRunner = NoTransaction) {}

  async park(v: Vehicle): Promise<Ticket> {
    return this.tx.run(() => {
      for (const floor of this.floors) {
        const allocator = this.allocators.get(floor.id) ?? FirstFit;
        let slot: Slot;
        try { slot = allocator.allocate(floor.slots, v); } catch { continue; }   // this floor is full
        slot.occupy(v);                                                           // ATOMIC
        floor.unindexFree(slot);
        this.trackColor(v, slot);
        const ticket = new Ticket(`T${++this.ticketSeq}`, slot.ref, this.clock.now());
        this.byTicket.set(ticket.id, { ticket, vehicle: v });
        return ticket;
      }
      throw new NoSlotAvailable(v.type);
    });
  }
  async unpark(ticketId: string): Promise<{ ticket: Ticket; vehicle: Vehicle; fee: number; hours: number }> {
    return this.tx.run(() => {
      const rec = this.byTicket.get(ticketId); if (!rec) throw new NoSuchTicket(ticketId);
      const floor = this.floors.find(f => f.id === rec.ticket.slot.floor)!;
      const slot = floor.slotAt(rec.ticket.slot);
      const vehicle = slot.vacate();                                             // FREE first
      floor.indexFree(slot);
      this.byColor.get(vehicle.color)?.delete(slot);
      this.byTicket.delete(ticketId);
      const hours = Math.max(1, Math.ceil((this.clock.now() - rec.ticket.issuedAt) / 3_600_000));  // round UP
      return { ticket: rec.ticket, vehicle, fee: this.rates[vehicle.type].feeFor(hours), hours };
    });
  }
  findFreeSlots(count: number, minSize: SlotSize = 'motorbike'): SlotRef[] {
    const min = SIZE_ORDER.indexOf(minSize), out: SlotRef[] = [];
    outer: for (const floor of this.floors)
      for (let i = min; i < SIZE_ORDER.length; i++)
        for (const s of floor.freeSlots(SIZE_ORDER[i]!)) {
          out.push(s.ref); if (out.length >= count) break outer;
        }
    return out;
  }
  findSlotsBySize(size: SlotSize) { return this.floors.flatMap(f => [...f.freeSlots(size)].map(s => s.ref)); }
  findVehiclesByColor(color: Color) { return [...(this.byColor.get(color) ?? [])].map(s => s.current!).filter(Boolean); }
  availability() {
    const out = new Map<SlotSize, number>(SIZE_ORDER.map(s => [s, 0]));
    this.floors.forEach(f => f.freeCountBySize().forEach((n, s) => out.set(s, out.get(s)! + n)));
    return out;
  }
  private trackColor(v: Vehicle, slot: Slot) {
    let set = this.byColor.get(v.color); if (!set) this.byColor.set(v.color, (set = new Set())); set.add(slot);
  }
}
export class SlotOccupied extends Error { constructor(r: SlotRef) { super(`slot ${JSON.stringify(r)} occupied`); } }
export class SlotAlreadyFree extends Error { constructor(r: SlotRef) { super(`slot ${JSON.stringify(r)} already free`); } }
export class VehicleTooLarge extends Error { constructor(v: VehicleType, s: SlotSize) { super(`${v} does not fit a ${s} slot`); } }
export class NoSlotAvailable extends Error { constructor(v?: VehicleType) { super(`no slot available${v ? ` for ${v}` : ''}`); } }
export class NoSlotAccessible extends Error { constructor(v: VehicleType) { super(`no accessible slot for ${v}`); } }
export class NoSlotEv extends Error { constructor(v: VehicleType) { super(`no EV slot for ${v}`); } }
export class NoSuchSlot extends Error { constructor(r: SlotRef) { super(`no such slot ${JSON.stringify(r)}`); } }
export class NoSuchTicket extends Error { constructor(id: string) { super(`no such ticket ${id}`); } }
export class InvalidPlate extends Error { constructor(p: string) { super(`invalid plate "${p}"`); } }
```

```ts
// ─────────────────────────── parking.test.ts ───────────────────────────
import { Floor, ParkingLot, Vehicle, FirstFit, HOURLY, NoSlotAvailable, SlotOccupied } from './parking';
let clockMs = 0; const clock = { now: () => clockMs };
const test = (name: string, fn: () => void | Promise<void>) =>
  Promise.resolve().then(fn).then(() => console.log('  ok', name),
    e => { console.error('  FAIL', name, (e as Error).message); process.exitCode = 1; });

await test('park then unpark charges by hours rounded up', async () => {
  const lot = new ParkingLot([new Floor(1, 1, 4)], new Map([[1, FirstFit]]), HOURLY, clock);
  const t = await lot.park(Vehicle.of('abc123', 'compact', 'red'));
  clockMs += 90 * 60 * 1000;                                 // 1.5 hours
  const r = await lot.unpark(t.id);
  if (r.hours !== 2) throw new Error(`hours should round up to 2, got ${r.hours}`);
  if (r.fee !== 600) throw new Error(`fee should be 600, got ${r.fee}`);
  if (lot.findFreeSlots(1).length !== 1) throw new Error('slot should be free again');
});
await test('a large vehicle only takes a large slot', async () => {
  const lot = new ParkingLot([new Floor(1, 1, 14)], new Map([[1, FirstFit]]), HOURLY, clock);
  await lot.park(Vehicle.of('big1', 'large', 'blue'));
  if (lot.findFreeSlots(1, 'large').length !== 0) throw new Error('all large slots should be consumed');
});
await test('a full lot raises NoSlotAvailable', async () => {
  const lot = new ParkingLot([new Floor(1, 1, 1)], new Map([[1, FirstFit]]), HOURLY, clock);
  await lot.park(Vehicle.of('aaa111', 'motorbike', 'red'));
  try { await lot.park(Vehicle.of('bbb222', 'motorbike', 'blue')); throw new Error('should have thrown'); }
  catch (e) { if (!(e instanceof NoSlotAvailable)) throw e; }
});
await test('the same slot cannot be double-occupied', () => {
  const floor = new Floor(1, 1, 2); const slot = floor.slots[0]!;
  slot.occupy(Vehicle.of('aaa111', 'motorbike', 'red'));
  try { slot.occupy(Vehicle.of('bbb222', 'motorbike', 'blue')); throw new Error('should have thrown'); }
  catch (e) { if (!(e instanceof SlotOccupied)) throw e; }
});
await test('findVehiclesByColor uses the index', async () => {
  const lot = new ParkingLot([new Floor(1, 1, 10)], new Map([[1, FirstFit]]), HOURLY, clock);
  await lot.park(Vehicle.of('aaa111', 'compact', 'red'));
  await lot.park(Vehicle.of('bbb222', 'compact', 'blue'));
  await lot.park(Vehicle.of('ccc333', 'large', 'red'));
  if (lot.findVehiclesByColor('red').length !== 2) throw new Error('expected 2 red');
  if (lot.findVehiclesByColor('green').length !== 0) throw new Error('expected 0 green');
});
await test('availability aggregates across floors', async () => {
  const lot = new ParkingLot([new Floor(1, 1, 6), new Floor(2, 1, 6)],
                              new Map([[1, FirstFit], [2, FirstFit]]), HOURLY, clock);
  const before = lot.availability().get('motorbike')!;
  await lot.park(Vehicle.of('aaa111', 'motorbike', 'red'));
  if (lot.availability().get('motorbike') !== before - 1) throw new Error('count should drop by 1');
});
```

**Follow-ups.** Concurrency (`Slot.occupy` as the critical section; in a real system a DB transaction and `UPDATE … WHERE occupant IS NULL` with a row-count check). Reservations adding a `RESERVED` state plus a hold expiry, competing for the same free-slot index. Occupancy analytics via events — the free-slot index is then a projection. Multi-lot networks (added latency, consistency gap).

---

## Problem 5 — Expense sharing with exact splits and debt simplification

**Difficulty:** 🟡 Intermediate · **Must-know**

**Requirement.** `addExpense`, `balances`, `settleUp` (minimal transfers), `deleteExpense` with correct ledger reversal; equal/exact/percentage/shares splits that always sum exactly to the total.

```ts
// ─────────────────────────── splitwise.ts ───────────────────────────
export class Money {
  private constructor(readonly minor: number, readonly currency: string) {}
  static of(minor: number, currency = 'USD'): Money {
    if (!Number.isSafeInteger(minor)) throw new NonIntegerAmount(minor);
    return new Money(minor, currency);
  }
  static zero(currency = 'USD') { return new Money(0, currency); }
  add(o: Money): Money {
    if (o.currency !== this.currency) throw new CurrencyMismatch(this.currency, o.currency);
    const s = this.minor + o.minor;
    if (!Number.isSafeInteger(s)) throw new AmountOverflow(s);
    return new Money(s, this.currency);
  }
  sub(o: Money) { return this.add(Money.of(-o.minor, o.currency)); }
  neg() { return Money.of(-this.minor, this.currency); }
  get isZero() { return this.minor === 0; }
  get positive() { return this.minor > 0; }
  cmp(o: Money) { if (o.currency !== this.currency) throw new CurrencyMismatch(this.currency, o.currency); return this.minor - o.minor; }
}
export interface SplitInput { exact?: Map<string, Money>; percentages?: Map<string, number>; weights?: Map<string, number>; }
export interface SplitStrategy { readonly name: string; shares(total: Money, participants: readonly string[], input?: SplitInput): Map<string, Money>; }

export const EqualSplit: SplitStrategy = {
  name: 'equal',
  shares(total, participants) {
    const n = participants.length;
    if (n === 0) throw new NoParticipants();
    if (new Set(participants).size !== n) throw new DuplicateParticipants();
    const base = Math.floor(total.minor / n);
    let remainder = total.minor - base * n;                   // 0..n-1 minor units
    const ordered = [...participants].sort();                 // deterministic tie-break
    const out = new Map<string, Money>();
    for (const p of ordered) {
      const extra = remainder > 0 ? 1 : 0;                    // one unit at a time until gone
      if (extra) remainder--;
      out.set(p, Money.of(base + extra, total.currency));
    }
    assertExact(out, total);
    return out;
  },
};
export const ExactSplit: SplitStrategy = {
  name: 'exact',
  shares(total, participants, input) {
    const m = new Map<string, Money>(input?.exact ?? []);
    for (const u of m.keys()) if (!participants.includes(u)) throw new UnknownParticipant(u);
    assertExact(m, total); return m;
  },
};
export const PercentageSplit: SplitStrategy = {
  name: 'percentage',
  shares(total, participants, input) {
    const pcts = input?.percentages;
    if (!pcts) throw new MissingSplitInput('percentages');
    const sum = [...pcts.values()].reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0);
    if (Math.abs(sum - 100) > 1e-9) throw new PercentagesDoNotSumTo100(sum);
    const out = new Map<string, Money>(); let allocated = 0;
    const entries = [...pcts.entries()].sort((a, b) => b[1] - a[1]);   // deterministic remainder order
    entries.forEach(([u, pct], i) => {
      const v = i === entries.length - 1 ? total.minor - allocated     // last absorbs the remainder
                                         : Math.round(total.minor * (pct / 100));
      allocated += v; out.set(u, Money.of(v, total.currency));
    });
    assertExact(out, total); return out;
  },
};
export const SharesSplit: SplitStrategy = {
  name: 'shares',
  shares(total, _p, input) {
    const w = input?.weights; if (!w) throw new MissingSplitInput('weights');
    const totalW = [...w.values()].reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0);
    if (totalW <= 0) throw new InvalidWeights();
    const out = new Map<string, Money>(); let allocated = 0;
    const entries = [...w.entries()].sort((a, b) => b[1] - a[1]);
    entries.forEach(([u, weight], i) => {
      const v = i === entries.length - 1 ? total.minor - allocated : Math.floor(total.minor * (weight / totalW));
      allocated += v; out.set(u, Money.of(v, total.currency));
    });
    assertExact(out, total); return out;
  },
};

export interface Expense { id: string; payer: string; total: Money; shares: Map<string, Money>; at: number; }
export class Ledger {
  private readonly net = new Map<string, Money>();
  constructor(readonly currency = 'USD') {}
  record(e: Expense) { this.credit(e.payer, e.total); for (const [u, s] of e.shares) this.debit(u, s); this.assertBalanced(); }
  unrecord(e: Expense) { this.debit(e.payer, e.total); for (const [u, s] of e.shares) this.credit(u, s); this.assertBalanced(); }
  balanceOf(u: string) { return this.net.get(u) ?? Money.zero(this.currency); }
  /** THE master invariant. If this fails, the whole model is corrupt. */
  assertBalanced(): void {
    const t = [...this.net.values()].reduce((acc, m) => acc.add(m), Money.zero(this.currency));
    if (!t.isZero) throw new LedgerNotBalanced(t.minor);
  }
  entries() { return this.net; }
  private credit(u: string, m: Money) { this.net.set(u, this.balanceOf(u).add(m)); }
  private debit(u: string, m: Money) { this.net.set(u, this.balanceOf(u).sub(m)); }
}
export class Splitwise {
  private readonly ledgers = new Map<string, Ledger>();
  private readonly expenses = new Map<string, Expense>();
  private readonly strategies: Record<string, SplitStrategy>;
  constructor(strategies: Record<string, SplitStrategy> = { equal: EqualSplit, exact: ExactSplit,
                                                           percentage: PercentageSplit, shares: SharesSplit }) {
    this.strategies = strategies;
  }
  private ledgerFor(g: string) { let l = this.ledgers.get(g); if (!l) this.ledgers.set(g, (l = new Ledger())); return l; }
  addExpense(e: { id: string; group: string; payer: string; total: Money; participants: readonly string[];
                  mode: string; at: number; input?: SplitInput }): Expense {
    const strategy = this.strategies[e.mode];
    if (!strategy) throw new UnknownSplitMode(e.mode);
    if (this.expenses.has(e.id)) throw new DuplicateExpenseId(e.id);
    const expense: Expense = { id: e.id, payer: e.payer, total: e.total,
                               shares: strategy.shares(e.total, e.participants, e.input), at: e.at };
    this.expenses.set(e.id, expense);
    this.ledgerFor(e.group).record(expense);
    return expense;
  }
  deleteExpense(group: string, id: string): void {
    const e = this.expenses.get(id); if (!e) throw new NoSuchExpense(id);
    this.ledgerFor(group).unrecord(e);              // reverse; never mutate in place
    this.expenses.delete(id);
  }
  balances(group: string) { return new Map(this.ledgerFor(group).entries()); }
  /** Greedy simplification: largest debtor ↔ largest creditor. ≤ n-1 transfers (not provably minimal). */
  settleUp(group: string): { from: string; to: string; amount: Money }[] {
    const debts = [...this.ledgerFor(group).entries()].filter(([, m]) => m.minor < 0)
      .map(([u, m]) => ({ u, v: -m.minor })).sort((a, b) => b.v - a.v);
    const credits = [...this.ledgerFor(group).entries()].filter(([, m]) => m.positive)
      .map(([u, m]) => ({ u, v: m.minor })).sort((a, b) => b.v - a.v);
    const out: { from: string; to: string; amount: Money }[] = [];
    let i = 0, j = 0;
    while (i < debts.length && j < credits.length) {
      const amt = Math.min(debts[i]!.v, credits[j]!.v);
      out.push({ from: debts[i]!.u, to: credits[j]!.u, amount: Money.of(amt) });
      debts[i]!.v -= amt; credits[j]!.v -= amt;
      if (debts[i]!.v === 0) i++;
      if (credits[j]!.v === 0) j++;
    }
    return out;
  }
}
function assertExact(shares: Map<string, Money>, total: Money): void {
  const sum = [...shares.values()].reduce((a, b) => a.add(b), Money.zero(total.currency));
  if (sum.cmp(total) !== 0) throw new SplitDoesNotSum(sum.minor, total.minor);
}
export class NonIntegerAmount extends Error { constructor(v: number) { super(`amount must be integer minor units, got ${v}`); } }
export class AmountOverflow extends Error { constructor(v: number) { super(`amount overflow: ${v}`); } }
export class CurrencyMismatch extends Error { constructor(a: string, b: string) { super(`${a} vs ${b}`); } }
export class LedgerNotBalanced extends Error { constructor(sum: number) { super(`ledger is not balanced: ${sum}`); } }
export class SplitDoesNotSum extends Error { constructor(a: number, b: number) { super(`shares sum to ${a}, expected ${b}`); } }
export class NoParticipants extends Error { constructor() { super('no participants'); } }
export class DuplicateParticipants extends Error { constructor() { super('duplicate participant ids'); } }
export class PercentagesDoNotSumTo100 extends Error { constructor(s: number) { super(`percentages sum to ${s}`); } }
export class InvalidWeights extends Error { constructor() { super('weights must be > 0'); } }
export class MissingSplitInput extends Error { constructor(k: string) { super(`missing split input: ${k}`); } }
export class UnknownParticipant extends Error { constructor(u: string) { super(`unknown participant ${u}`); } }
export class UnknownSplitMode extends Error { constructor(m: string) { super(`unknown split mode ${m}`); } }
export class DuplicateExpenseId extends Error { constructor(id: string) { super(`duplicate expense ${id}`); } }
export class NoSuchExpense extends Error { constructor(id: string) { super(`no such expense ${id}`); } }
```

```ts
// ─────────────────────────── splitwise.test.ts ───────────────────────────
import { Splitwise, Money, PercentagesDoNotSumTo100, LedgerNotBalanced } from './splitwise';
const test = (name: string, fn: () => void) =>
  Promise.resolve().then(fn).then(() => console.log('  ok', name),
    e => { console.error('  FAIL', name, (e as Error).message); process.exitCode = 1; });

test('equal split of 100 across 3 sums exactly', () => {
  const s = new Splitwise();
  const e = s.addExpense({ id: 'e1', group: 'g1', payer: 'alice', total: Money.of(100),
                           participants: ['bob', 'carol', 'dave'], mode: 'equal', at: 0 });
  const sum = [...e.shares.values()].reduce((a, b) => a.add(b), Money.zero());
  if (!sum.isZero) throw new Error('shares must sum to 100');
});
test('the ledger credits the payer and debits participants', () => {
  const s = new Splitwise();
  s.addExpense({ id: 'e1', group: 'g', payer: 'alice', total: Money.of(900),
                 participants: ['bob', 'carol'], mode: 'equal', at: 0 });
  const b = s.balances('g');
  if (b.get('alice')!.minor !== 900) throw new Error('alice should be credited 900');
  if (b.get('bob')!.minor !== -450) throw new Error('bob should owe 450');
});
test('delete reverses the ledger', () => {
  const s = new Splitwise();
  s.addExpense({ id: 'e1', group: 'g', payer: 'alice', total: Money.of(900),
                 participants: ['bob', 'carol'], mode: 'equal', at: 0 });
  s.deleteExpense('g', 'e1');
  for (const m of s.balances('g').values()) if (!m.isZero) throw new Error('all balances should be zero');
});
test('settleUp produces <= n-1 transfers and zeroes everyone', () => {
  const s = new Splitwise();
  s.addExpense({ id: 'e1', group: 'g', payer: 'a', total: Money.of(300), participants: ['a','b','c','d'], mode: 'equal', at: 0 });
  s.addExpense({ id: 'e2', group: 'g', payer: 'b', total: Money.of(500), participants: ['a','b'], mode: 'equal', at: 1 });
  const transfers = s.settleUp('g');
  if (transfers.length > 3) throw new Error(`expected <= 3 transfers, got ${transfers.length}`);
  const net = new Map([...s.balances('g')].map(([u, m]) => [u, m.minor] as [string, number]));
  for (const t of transfers) { net.set(t.from, net.get(t.from)! + t.amount.minor); net.set(t.to, net.get(t.to)! - t.amount.minor); }
  for (const [u, v] of net) if (Math.abs(v) > 1) throw new Error(`${u} not settled: ${v}`);
});
test('percentages that do not sum to 100 are rejected', () => {
  const s = new Splitwise();
  try {
    s.addExpense({ id: 'e1', group: 'g', payer: 'a', total: Money.of(1000), participants: ['a','b'],
                   mode: 'percentage', at: 0, input: { percentages: new Map([['a', 60], ['b', 30]]) } });
    throw new Error('should have thrown');
  } catch (err) { if (!(err instanceof PercentagesDoNotSumTo100)) throw err; }
});
test('the ledger invariant is enforced (corruption is detected)', () => {
  const s = new Splitwise();
  s.addExpense({ id: 'e1', group: 'g', payer: 'a', total: Money.of(100), participants: ['b'], mode: 'equal', at: 0 });
  s.balances('g').set('a', Money.of(1));
  try { s.deleteExpense('g', 'e1'); throw new Error('should have detected corruption'); }
  catch (e) { if (!(e instanceof LedgerNotBalanced)) throw e; }
});
console.log('splitwise tests done');
```

**Follow-ups.** Multi-currency (store the FX rate + timestamp per expense, or per-currency ledgers; never revalue history at today's rate). Exact minimal settlement (greedy is not provably minimal; exhaustive search for small n, max-flow for larger). Rounding fairness (a fixed tie-break can be gamed; consider a rotation and document it).

## Problem 6 — Logger with async batching, redaction, dedupe, and correlation

**Difficulty:** 🟡 Intermediate · **Must-know**

**Requirement.** Levels, structured fields, child loggers, async batched fan-out, bounded buffer with a drop policy, error dedupe, redaction at the sink layer, per-namespace levels.

```ts
// ─────────────────────────── logger.ts ───────────────────────────
export type Level = 'trace' | 'debug' | 'info' | 'warn' | 'error' | 'fatal';
export const LEVEL_VALUE: Record<Level, number> = { trace: 10, debug: 20, info: 30, warn: 40, error: 50, fatal: 60 };
export type Fields = Record<string, unknown>;
export interface LogRecord { ts: string; level: Level; msg: string; ns: string; fields: Fields; traceId?: string; }
export interface LogSink { readonly name: string; writeBatch(r: LogRecord[]): void; flush?(): Promise<void>; close?(): Promise<void>; }

const REDACT = /^(password|passwd|token|secret|apiKey|api_key|authorization|cookie|set-cookie|card|cardNumber|cvv|cvc|ssn|pin)$/i;
export class RedactingSink implements LogSink {
  readonly name = 'redacting';
  constructor(private readonly inner: LogSink) {}
  writeBatch(records: LogRecord[]): void {
    this.inner.writeBatch(records.map(r => ({
      ...r,
      msg: r.msg.replace(/[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+/g, '[email]')
                  .replace(/\b\d{12,19}\b/g, '[pan]')
                  .replace(/Bearer\s+[\w.\-]+/gi, 'Bearer [redacted]'),
      fields: redactFields(r.fields),
    })));
  }
  flush() { return this.inner.flush?.(); }
  close() { return this.inner.close?.(); }
}
function redactFields(f: Fields): Fields {
  const out: Fields = {};
  for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(f)) {
    if (REDACT.test(k)) { out[k] = '[redacted]'; continue; }
    out[k] = v && typeof v === 'object' && !Array.isArray(v) && !(v instanceof Date)
      ? redactFields(v as Fields)
      : typeof v === 'string' ? v.replace(/[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+/g, '[email]') : v;
  }
  return out;
}
export class RepeatDedupe {
  private readonly seen = new Map<string, { count: number; last: number }>();
  constructor(private readonly windowMs = 3000, private readonly threshold = 5, private readonly now = () => Date.now()) {}
  apply(r: LogRecord): boolean {
    const key = `${r.level}|${r.ns}|${r.msg}`;
    const t = this.now(), e = this.seen.get(key);
    if (!e) { this.seen.set(key, { count: 1, last: t }); return true; }
    if (t - e.last > this.windowMs) { e.count = 1; e.last = t; return true; }
    e.count++; e.last = t;
    if (e.count <= this.threshold) return true;
    if (e.count === this.threshold + 1)
      r.fields = { ...r.fields, suppressedRepeats: e.count, note: 'further identical records suppressed for the window' };
    return false;
  }
}
export class LogPipeline {
  private buffer: LogRecord[] = [];
  private draining = false; private timer?: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout>;
  private dropped = 0;
  constructor(private readonly sinks: LogSink[],
              private readonly opts: { batchSize?: number; flushMs?: number; maxBuffer?: number;
                                      shouldLevel?: (l: Level, ns: string) => boolean;
                                      dedupe?: RepeatDedupe } = {}) {}
  get droppedCount() { return this.dropped; }
  log(r: LogRecord): void {
    try {                                                      // logging must never throw
      if (this.opts.shouldLevel && !this.opts.shouldLevel(r.level, r.ns)) return;   // EARLY EXIT
      if (this.opts.dedupe && !this.opts.dedupe.apply(r)) return;
      if (this.buffer.length >= (this.opts.maxBuffer ?? 10_000)) { this.evictLowest(); this.dropped++; }
      this.buffer.push(r);
      if (this.buffer.length >= (this.opts.batchSize ?? 200)) void this.drain();
      else if (!this.timer) this.timer = setTimeout(() => { this.timer = undefined; void this.drain(); },
                                                    this.opts.flushMs ?? 1000);
    } catch { /* swallow: a logger that breaks the app is worse than one that loses a line */ }
  }
  async drain(): Promise<void> {                               // SINGLE-FLIGHT
    if (this.draining) return;
    this.draining = true;
    const batch = this.buffer.splice(0, this.buffer.length);
    try { await Promise.allSettled(this.sinks.map(s => { s.writeBatch(batch); return s.flush?.() ?? Promise.resolve(); })); }
    finally {
      this.draining = false;
      if (this.buffer.length) this.timer = setTimeout(() => { this.timer = undefined; void this.drain(); },
                                                       this.opts.flushMs ?? 1000);
    }
  }
  async close(): Promise<void> { await this.drain(); await Promise.allSettled(this.sinks.map(s => s.close?.() ?? Promise.resolve())); }
  private evictLowest(): void {
    let idx = 0;
    for (let i = 1; i < this.buffer.length; i++)
      if (LEVEL_VALUE[this.buffer[i]!.level] < LEVEL_VALUE[this.buffer[idx]!.level]) idx = i;
    this.buffer.splice(idx, 1);
  }
}
export class LevelConfig {
  private rules: Record<string, number> = {};
  private def: number;
  constructor(defaultLevel: Level = 'info') { this.def = LEVEL_VALUE[defaultLevel]; }
  setDefault(l: Level) { this.def = LEVEL_VALUE[l]; }
  setNamespace(ns: string, l: Level) { this.rules[ns] = LEVEL_VALUE[l]; }
  allows(l: Level, ns: string): boolean {
    let threshold = this.def;                                 // most specific namespace wins
    for (const key of Object.keys(this.rules)) if (ns === key || ns.startsWith(`${key}.`)) threshold = this.rules[key]!;
    return LEVEL_VALUE[l] >= threshold;
  }
}
export interface Logger {
  readonly ns: string;
  trace(m: string, f?: Fields): void; debug(m: string, f?: Fields): void; info(m: string, f?: Fields): void;
  warn(m: string, f?: Fields): void; error(m: string, f?: Fields): void; fatal(m: string, f?: Fields): void;
  child(ns: string, f?: Fields): Logger;
}
class LoggerImpl implements Logger {
  constructor(readonly ns: string, private readonly base: Fields, private readonly pipeline: LogPipeline,
              private readonly should: (l: Level, ns: string) => boolean, private readonly now: () => number) {}
  private write(level: Level, msg: string, f?: Fields): void {
    if (!this.should(level, this.ns)) return;
    this.pipeline.log({ ts: new Date(this.now()).toISOString(), level, msg, ns: this.ns,
                        fields: { ...this.base, ...f }, traceId: this.base.traceId as string | undefined });
  }
  trace(m: string, f?: Fields) { this.write('trace', m, f); }
  debug(m: string, f?: Fields) { this.write('debug', m, f); }
  info(m: string, f?: Fields)  { this.write('info', m, f); }
  warn(m: string, f?: Fields)  { this.write('warn', m, f); }
  error(m: string, f?: Fields) { this.write('error', m, f); }
  fatal(m: string, f?: Fields) { this.write('fatal', m, f); }
  child(ns: string, f?: Fields) {
    return new LoggerImpl(`${this.ns}.${ns}`, { ...this.base, ...f }, this.pipeline, this.should, this.now);
  }
}
export function createLogger(opts: { sinks: LogSink[]; levels?: LevelConfig; base?: Fields;
                                    batchSize?: number; flushMs?: number; now?: () => number }): Logger & { pipeline: LogPipeline } {
  const levels = opts.levels ?? new LevelConfig();
  const now = opts.now ?? Date.now;
  const pipeline = new LogPipeline(opts.sinks.map(s => new RedactingSink(s)),
    { shouldLevel: (l, ns) => levels.allows(l, ns), batchSize: opts.batchSize, flushMs: opts.flushMs });
  return Object.assign(new LoggerImpl('app', opts.base ?? {}, pipeline, (l, ns) => levels.allows(l, ns), now), { pipeline });
}
export class MemorySink implements LogSink {
  readonly name = 'memory'; readonly records: LogRecord[] = [];
  writeBatch(rs: LogRecord[]) { this.records.push(...rs); }
}
export class NdjsonSink implements LogSink {
  readonly name = 'ndjson';
  constructor(private readonly write: (line: string) => void = l => process.stdout.write(l)) {}
  writeBatch(rs: LogRecord[]) { for (const r of rs) this.write(JSON.stringify(r) + '\n'); }
}
```

```ts
// ─────────────────────────── logger.test.ts ───────────────────────────
import { createLogger, MemorySink, LevelConfig, LogRecord } from './logger';
const test = (name: string, fn: () => void | Promise<void>) =>
  Promise.resolve().then(fn).then(() => console.log('  ok', name),
    e => { console.error('  FAIL', name, (e as Error).message); process.exitCode = 1; });

await test('levels filter before records are created', async () => {
  const sink = new MemorySink();
  const log = createLogger({ sinks: [sink], levels: new LevelConfig('warn') });
  log.debug('nope'); log.info('nope'); log.warn('yes'); log.error('yes too');
  await log.pipeline.drain();
  if (sink.records.length !== 2) throw new Error(`expected 2 records, got ${sink.records.length}`);
});
await test('per-namespace levels allow a debug flag in one module only', async () => {
  const sink = new MemorySink(); const levels = new LevelConfig('error');
  levels.setNamespace('order', 'trace');
  const log = createLogger({ sinks: [sink], levels });
  log.child('order', { traceId: 't1' }).trace('verbose order detail');
  log.child('payment').trace('suppressed');
  await log.pipeline.drain();
  if (sink.records.length !== 1) throw new Error(`expected 1, got ${sink.records.length}`);
  if (sink.records[0]!.ns !== 'app.order') throw new Error('namespace not composed');
  if (sink.records[0]!.traceId !== 't1') throw new Error('child fields not inherited');
});
await test('redaction happens in the sink layer', async () => {
  const captured: LogRecord[] = [];
  const sink = { name: 'capture', writeBatch: (rs: LogRecord[]) => { captured.push(...rs); } };
  const log = createLogger({ sinks: [sink] });
  log.info('login for alice@example.com', { password: 'hunter2', token: 'abc.def', user: { email: 'bob@example.com', id: 7 } });
  await log.pipeline.drain();
  const blob = JSON.stringify(captured[0]);
  if (blob.includes('hunter2')) throw new Error('password leaked');
  if (blob.includes('alice@example.com')) throw new Error('email leaked');
  if (captured[0]!.fields.password !== '[redacted]') throw new Error('password not redacted');
  if ((captured[0]!.fields.user as any).id !== 7) throw new Error('non-sensitive field must survive');
});
await test('a bounded buffer drops the lowest severity and counts it', () => {
  const log = createLogger({ sinks: [], maxBuffer: 5, batchSize: 1000, flushMs: 1_000_000 });
  for (let i = 0; i < 20; i++) log.info(`flood ${i}`);
  log.fatal('keep me');
  if (log.pipeline.droppedCount < 14) throw new Error(`unexpected drop count ${log.pipeline.droppedCount}`);
});
await test('a failing sink does not break the others or throw', async () => {
  const good = new MemorySink();
  const bad = { name: 'bad', writeBatch: () => { throw new Error('sink exploded'); } };
  const log = createLogger({ sinks: [bad, good] });
  log.info('hello');
  await log.pipeline.drain();
  if (good.records.length !== 1) throw new Error('the good sink should still receive the record');
});
await test('child loggers compose namespaces and merge fields', async () => {
  const sink = new MemorySink();
  const log = createLogger({ sinks: [sink], base: { env: 'test', app: 'billing' } });
  log.child('http').child('handler').warn('slow request', { ms: 1200 });
  await log.pipeline.drain();
  const r = sink.records[0]!;
  if (r.ns !== 'app.http.handler') throw new Error(`ns was ${r.ns}`);
  if (r.fields.env !== 'test' || r.fields.ms !== 1200) throw new Error('fields not merged');
});
console.log('logger tests done');
```

**Follow-ups.** Sampling (by level/namespace/percentage; never sample `error+`). Cost control (drop policy, dedupe, disciplined levels). Correlation without parameter threading (`AsyncLocalStorage` or the OTel context). Ordering is not guaranteed across sinks or processes — never assert on log order in a test. Hot-reloadable levels are how you debug a production incident.

## Problem 7 — Circuit breaker + retry with backoff/jitter + bulkhead, composed correctly

**Difficulty:** 🔴 Advanced · **Must-know**

**Requirement.** Breaker with closed/open/half-open and a failure ratio; retry with exponential backoff + full jitter and a time budget; a bulkhead; and the correct composition so retries do not multiply.

```ts
// ─────────────────────────── resilience.ts ───────────────────────────
export class CircuitOpenError extends Error { constructor(public readonly until: number) { super('circuit open'); this.name = 'CircuitOpenError'; } }
export type BreakerState = 'closed' | 'open' | 'half-open';
export interface BreakerConfig {
  failureRatio?: number; minSamples?: number; successThreshold?: number;
  openMs: number; halfOpenMax?: number;
  classify?: (err: unknown) => boolean;             // true = counts as a dependency failure
}
export class CircuitBreaker {
  private state: BreakerState = 'closed';
  private failures = 0; private successes = 0; private total = 0; private openedAt = 0; private probes = 0;
  constructor(private readonly cfg: BreakerConfig, private readonly now: () => number = Date.now) {}
  get snapshot() { return { state: this.state, failures: this.failures, total: this.total }; }
  get currentState() { return this.state; }
  async call<T>(fn: () => Promise<T>, fallback?: (err: unknown) => T): Promise<T> {
    this.tick();
    if (this.state === 'open') throw new CircuitOpenError(this.openedAt + this.cfg.openMs);   // FAIL FAST
    if (this.state === 'half-open' && this.probes >= (this.cfg.halfOpenMax ?? 1)) throw new CircuitOpenError(this.now());
    if (this.state === 'half-open') this.probes++;
    try {
      const v = await fn(); this.onSuccess(); return v;
    } catch (e) {
      if (this.cfg.classify ? this.cfg.classify(e) : true) this.onFailure();
      if (fallback) return fallback(e);
      throw e;
    } finally { if (this.state === 'half-open') this.probes--; }
  }
  private tick(): void {
    if (this.state === 'open' && this.now() - this.openedAt >= this.cfg.openMs) {
      this.state = 'half-open'; this.successes = 0; this.probes = 0; this.total = 0;
    }
  }
  private onSuccess(): void {
    this.total++;
    if (this.state === 'half-open') {
      if (++this.successes >= (this.cfg.successThreshold ?? 2)) { this.state = 'closed'; this.failures = 0; this.successes = 0; this.total = 0; }
    } else this.failures = 0;
  }
  private onFailure(): void {
    this.total++; this.failures++;
    if (this.state === 'half-open') { this.open(); return; }
    if (this.total >= (this.cfg.minSamples ?? 10) && this.failures / this.total >= (this.cfg.failureRatio ?? 0.5)) this.open();
  }
  private open(): void { this.state = 'open'; this.openedAt = this.now(); this.successes = 0; }
}
export interface RetryConfig {
  maxAttempts: number; baseMs: number; maxMs: number; budgetMs: number;
  retryable?: (err: unknown) => boolean; rand?: () => number; sleep?: (ms: number) => Promise<void>;
}
export class RetryBudgetExhausted extends Error { constructor() { super('retry budget exhausted'); } }
export function withRetry<T>(fn: () => Promise<T>, cfg: RetryConfig): Promise<T> {
  const rand = cfg.rand ?? Math.random;
  const sleep = cfg.sleep ?? ((ms: number) => new Promise<void>(r => setTimeout(r, ms)));
  const started = Date.now();
  const attempt = async (n: number): Promise<T> => {
    try { return await fn(); }
    catch (e) {
      if (n >= cfg.maxAttempts) throw e;
      if (cfg.retryable && !cfg.retryable(e)) throw e;
      if (cfg.budgetMs - (Date.now() - started) <= 0) throw new RetryBudgetExhausted();
      await sleep(Math.round(rand() * Math.min(cfg.maxMs, cfg.baseMs * 2 ** (n - 1))));  // FULL JITTER
      return attempt(n + 1);
    }
  };
  return attempt(1);
}
export class Bulkhead {
  private available: number; private readonly waiters: (() => void)[] = [];
  constructor(private readonly capacity: number, private readonly queueLimit = 0) {
    if (capacity < 1) throw new RangeError('capacity must be >= 1');
    this.available = capacity;
  }
  async acquire(): Promise<() => void> {
    if (this.available > 0) { this.available--; return this.release(); }
    if (this.queueLimit === 0) throw new BulkheadFull('no queue: fail fast');
    if (this.waiters.length >= this.queueLimit) throw new BulkheadFull('queue full');
    return new Promise(res => this.waiters.push(() => { this.available--; res(this.release()); }));
  }
  private release(): () => void {
    let done = false;
    return () => { if (done) return; done = true; this.available++; const n = this.waiters.shift(); if (n) n(); };
  }
}
export class BulkheadFull extends Error {}
export class TimeoutError extends Error { constructor(ms: number) { super(`timed out after ${ms}ms`); } }
export function withTimeout<T>(p: Promise<T>, ms: number): Promise<T> {
  return new Promise<T>((resolve, reject) => {
    const t = setTimeout(() => reject(new TimeoutError(ms)), ms);
    p.then(v => { clearTimeout(t); resolve(v); }, e => { clearTimeout(t); reject(e); });
  });
}
/**
 * Correct composition: the BREAKER wraps the RETRY so it observes one logical outcome per caller,
 * and the BULKHEAD bounds in-flight work so a slow dependency cannot exhaust the shared pool.
 * The retry budget must be smaller than the caller's deadline.
 */
export async function callDependency<T>(fn: () => Promise<T>, opts: {
  breaker: CircuitBreaker; retry: RetryConfig; bulkhead: Bulkhead; fallback?: (e: unknown) => T }): Promise<T> {
  const release = await opts.bulkhead.acquire();
  try { return await opts.breaker.call(() => withRetry(fn, opts.retry), opts.fallback as any); }
  finally { release(); }
}
```

```ts
// ─────────────────────────── resilience.test.ts ───────────────────────────
import { CircuitBreaker, CircuitOpenError, Bulkhead, BulkheadFull, withRetry, RetryBudgetExhausted,
         TimeoutError, withTimeout } from './resilience';
const test = (name: string, fn: () => void | Promise<void>) =>
  Promise.resolve().then(fn).then(() => console.log('  ok', name),
    e => { console.error('  FAIL', name, (e as Error).message); process.exitCode = 1; });

await test('the breaker opens at the failure ratio and then fails fast', async () => {
  let now = 0; let calls = 0;
  const b = new CircuitBreaker({ failureRatio: 0.5, minSamples: 4, openMs: 1000, successThreshold: 2 }, () => now);
  const failing = () => { calls++; throw new Error('down'); };
  for (let i = 0; i < 4; i++) await b.call(failing).catch(() => {});
  if (b.currentState !== 'open') throw new Error(`expected open, got ${b.currentState}`);
  await b.call(failing).catch(e => { if (!(e instanceof CircuitOpenError)) throw e; });
  if (calls !== 4) throw new Error('an open breaker must not call the dependency');
});
await test('half-open closes after enough successful probes', async () => {
  let now = 0, healthy = false;
  const b = new CircuitBreaker({ failureRatio: 0.5, minSamples: 4, openMs: 1000, successThreshold: 2 }, () => now);
  const call = async () => { if (!healthy) throw new Error('down'); return 'ok'; };
  for (let i = 0; i < 4; i++) await b.call(call).catch(() => {});
  now += 1001; healthy = true;
  await b.call(call); await b.call(call);
  if (b.currentState !== 'closed') throw new Error(`expected closed, got ${b.currentState}`);
});
await test('client errors do not trip the breaker', async () => {
  let now = 0;
  class ValidationError extends Error {}
  const b = new CircuitBreaker({ failureRatio: 0.5, minSamples: 3, openMs: 1000,
                                 classify: e => !(e instanceof ValidationError) }, () => now);
  for (let i = 0; i < 10; i++) await b.call(() => { throw new ValidationError('bad input'); }).catch(() => {});
  if (b.currentState !== 'closed') throw new Error('4xx must not trip the breaker');
});
await test('retry uses full jitter and doubles the backoff', async () => {
  let attempts = 0; const delays: number[] = [];
  await withRetry(() => { attempts++; throw new Error('flaky'); },
    { maxAttempts: 4, baseMs: 100, maxMs: 1000, budgetMs: 10_000, retryable: () => true,
      rand: () => 0.5, sleep: async ms => { delays.push(ms); } }).catch(() => {});
  if (attempts !== 4) throw new Error(`expected 4 attempts, got ${attempts}`);
  if (delays.join(',') !== '50,100,200') throw new Error(`unexpected delays ${delays}`);
});
await test('non-retryable errors are not retried', async () => {
  let attempts = 0;
  await withRetry(() => { attempts++; throw new Error('fatal'); },
    { maxAttempts: 5, baseMs: 1, maxMs: 10, budgetMs: 1000, retryable: () => false }).catch(() => {});
  if (attempts !== 1) throw new Error('should not retry');
});
await test('the budget can stop retries before maxAttempts', async () => {
  let attempts = 0; let fakeTime = 0;
  await withRetry(() => { attempts++; throw new Error('flaky'); },
    { maxAttempts: 10, baseMs: 10, maxMs: 1000, budgetMs: 25, rand: () => 0.1,
      retryable: () => true, sleep: async ms => { fakeTime += ms; } }).catch(e => {
      if (!(e instanceof RetryBudgetExhausted)) throw e;
    });
  if (attempts >= 10) throw new Error('budget should have stopped retries earlier');
});
await test('the bulkhead fails fast when saturated', async () => {
  const b = new Bulkhead(1, 0); const release = await b.acquire();
  try { await b.acquire(); throw new Error('should have thrown BulkheadFull'); }
  catch (e) { if (!(e instanceof BulkheadFull)) throw e; }
  release(); await b.acquire();
});
await test('the bulkhead bounds concurrency so one dependency cannot exhaust the pool', async () => {
  const bulkhead = new Bulkhead(2, 0);
  let inFlight = 0, maxInFlight = 0;
  const work = async () => {
    const release = await bulkhead.acquire();
    inFlight++; maxInFlight = Math.max(maxInFlight, inFlight);
    await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 5));
    inFlight--; release();
  };
  const results = await Promise.allSettled(Array.from({ length: 10 }, work));
  if (maxInFlight > 2) throw new Error(`concurrency cap breached: ${maxInFlight}`);
  if (results.filter(r => r.status === 'fulfilled').length !== 2) throw new Error('only 2 should succeed');
});
await test('timeout rejects', async () => {
  try { await withTimeout(new Promise<string>(r => setTimeout(() => r('late'), 50)), 5); throw new Error('no timeout'); }
  catch (e) { if (!(e instanceof TimeoutError)) throw e; }
});
console.log('resilience tests done');
```

**Follow-ups.** Where the breaker sits relative to the retry (outside, so it counts one logical outcome per caller, and a caller's deadline is the outer budget). Never retry non-idempotent writes without an idempotency key. Metrics: breaker transitions, rejections, fallbacks, retries, timeouts — a dashboard flat for a month is either stable or broken.

## Problem 8 — Dependency injection container with lifetimes and cycle detection

**Difficulty:** 🟡 Intermediate · **Must-know**

**Requirement.** Constructor wiring, three lifetimes (transient/singleton/scoped), per-request scoped storage, cycle detection with a clear message, and a manual composition root for comparison.

```ts
// ─────────────────────────── di.ts ───────────────────────────
export type Ctor<T> = abstract new (...args: any[]) => T;
export type Token<T> = symbol | Ctor<T>;
export type Lifetime = 'transient' | 'singleton' | 'scoped';
export class NoRegistrationError extends Error { constructor(t: unknown) { super(`no registration for ${String(t)}`); } }
export class CircularDependencyError extends Error { constructor(cycle: string[]) { super(`circular dependency: ${cycle.join(' -> ')}`); } }

interface Registration<T> { factory: (c: Container) => T; lifetime: Lifetime; }

export class Container {
  private readonly factories = new Map<unknown, Registration<unknown>>();
  private readonly singletons = new Map<unknown, { value: unknown }>();
  private scoped = new Map<unknown, unknown>();
  private readonly building: unknown[] = [];

  register<T>(token: Token<T>, factory: (c: Container) => T, lifetime: Lifetime = 'transient'): this {
    this.factories.set(token as unknown, { factory: factory as any, lifetime });
    return this;
  }
  resolve<T>(token: Token<T>): T {
    const reg = this.factories.get(token as unknown);
    if (!reg) throw new NoRegistrationError(token);
    const cached = this.singletons.get(token as unknown);
    if (cached) return cached.value as T;
    if (this.scoped.has(token as unknown)) return this.scoped.get(token as unknown) as T;
    if (this.building.includes(token as unknown))
      throw new CircularDependencyError(this.building.map(t => String(t)).concat(String(token)));
    this.building.push(token as unknown);
    try {
      const value = reg.factory(this);
      if (reg.lifetime === 'singleton') this.singletons.set(token as unknown, { value });
      else if (reg.lifetime === 'scoped') this.scoped.set(token as unknown, value);
      return value;
    } finally { this.building.pop(); }        // ALWAYS: a throwing factory must not poison the graph
  }
  has(token: Token<unknown>) { return this.factories.has(token as unknown); }
  /** Run `fn` inside a fresh scope — request-scoped lifetimes are per invocation. */
  async runScoped<T>(fn: (c: Container) => Promise<T> | T): Promise<T> {
    const saved = this.scoped;
    this.scoped = new Map();
    try { return await fn(this); } finally { this.scoped = saved; }
  }
}

// ── Example wiring ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
export interface Clock { now(): Date }
export interface Logger { log(m: string): void }
export interface OrderRepository { save(id: string): Promise<void> }
export interface PaymentGateway { charge(id: string, amountCents: number, key: string): Promise<{ ok: boolean }> }

class SystemClock implements Clock { now() { return new Date(); } }
class ConsoleLogger implements Logger { log(m: string) { console.log('[log]', m); } }
class RequestId { constructor(readonly value: string) {} }                                    // scoped
class SqlOrderRepo implements OrderRepository {
  constructor(private readonly dbUrl: string) {}
  async save(id: string) { void id; void this.dbUrl; }
}
class StripeGateway implements PaymentGateway {
  constructor(private readonly apiKey: string, private readonly clock: Clock) {}
  async charge(id: string, amountCents: number, key: string) { void id; void this.apiKey; void this.clock; void key; return { ok: amountCents > 0 }; }
}
export class OrderService {
  constructor(readonly repo: OrderRepository, readonly payments: PaymentGateway, readonly clock: Clock,
              readonly log: Logger, readonly requestId: RequestId) {}
}
const T = { OrderRepository: Symbol('OrderRepository'), PaymentGateway: Symbol('PaymentGateway'),
            Clock: Symbol('Clock'), Logger: Symbol('Logger'), OrderService: Symbol('OrderService'),
            RequestId: Symbol('RequestId') } as const;

export function buildContainer(env: { DB_URL: string; STRIPE_KEY: string }): Container {
  const c = new Container();
  c.register(T.Logger, () => new ConsoleLogger(), 'singleton');
  c.register(T.Clock, () => new SystemClock(), 'singleton');
  c.register(T.RequestId, () => new RequestId(Math.random().toString(36).slice(2)), 'scoped');
  c.register(T.OrderRepository, () => new SqlOrderRepo(env.DB_URL), 'singleton');
  c.register(T.PaymentGateway, cc => new StripeGateway(env.STRIPE_KEY, cc.resolve(T.Clock)), 'singleton');
  c.register(T.OrderService, cc => new OrderService(
    cc.resolve(T.OrderRepository), cc.resolve(T.PaymentGateway), cc.resolve(T.Clock),
    cc.resolve(T.Logger), cc.resolve(T.RequestId)), 'transient');
  return c;
}
/** Usually the better answer for application code: greppable, typed, debuggable. */
export function buildOrderServiceManually(env: { DB_URL: string; STRIPE_KEY: string }, requestId: RequestId): OrderService {
  const clock: Clock = new SystemClock();
  const log: Logger = new ConsoleLogger();
  const repo: OrderRepository = new SqlOrderRepo(env.DB_URL);
  const payments: PaymentGateway = new StripeGateway(env.STRIPE_KEY, clock);
  return new OrderService(repo, payments, clock, log, requestId);
}
```

```ts
// ─────────────────────────── di.test.ts ───────────────────────────
import { Container, CircularDependencyError, NoRegistrationError } from './di';
const TA = Symbol('A'), TB = Symbol('B');
const test = (name: string, fn: () => void | Promise<void>) =>
  Promise.resolve().then(fn).then(() => console.log('  ok', name),
    e => { console.error('  FAIL', name, (e as Error).message); process.exitCode = 1; });

await test('singleton resolves once', () => {
  const c = new Container(); let built = 0;
  c.register(TA, () => { built++; return { name: 'a' }; }, 'singleton');
  const x = c.resolve<{ name: string }>(TA), y = c.resolve<{ name: string }>(TA);
  if (built !== 1) throw new Error(`built ${built} times`);
  if (x !== y) throw new Error('singleton must be the same instance');
});
await test('transient resolves every time', () => {
  const c = new Container(); c.register(TA, () => ({ name: 'a' }), 'transient');
  if (c.resolve(TA) === c.resolve(TA)) throw new Error('transient must be new each time');
});
await test('scoped lifetime is per runScoped', async () => {
  const c = new Container(); c.register(TA, () => ({ name: 'a' }), 'scoped');
  const in1 = await c.runScoped(cc => cc.resolve(TA));
  const in2 = await c.runScoped(cc => cc.resolve(TA));
  if (in1 === in2) throw new Error('scoped must differ across scopes');
});
await test('circular dependency is reported clearly', () => {
  const c = new Container();
  c.register(TA, cc => ({ name: 'a', b: cc.resolve(TB) }));
  c.register(TB, cc => ({ name: 'b', a: cc.resolve(TA) }));
  try { c.resolve(TA); throw new Error('should have thrown'); }
  catch (e) { if (!(e instanceof CircularDependencyError)) throw e;
              if (!/A.*B.*A/.test((e as Error).message)) throw new Error(`unclear: ${(e as Error).message}`); }
});
await test('a throwing factory does not poison later resolutions', () => {
  const c = new Container(); let attempt = 0;
  c.register(TA, () => { attempt++; if (attempt === 1) throw new Error('first fails'); return { name: 'ok' }; });
  try { c.resolve(TA); } catch {}
  if (c.resolve<{ name: string }>(TA).name !== 'ok') throw new Error('second attempt should succeed');
});
await test('missing registration fails loudly', () => {
  const c = new Container();
  try { c.resolve(Symbol('nope')); throw new Error('should have thrown'); }
  catch (e) { if (!(e instanceof NoRegistrationError)) throw e; }
});
await test('a scope is restored even if the work throws', async () => {
  const c = new Container(); c.register(TA, () => ({ name: 'a' }), 'scoped');
  await c.runScoped(async () => { throw new Error('boom'); }).catch(() => {});
  if (c.has(TA) !== true) throw new Error('registration should persist after a failed scope');
});
console.log('DI tests done');
```

**Follow-ups.** Why not a container for application code (composition root is greppable, typed, debuggable; containers are for plugins, per-tenant bindings, frameworks). Scoping a transaction per request (scoped container + registered transaction + disposal at request end). Never injecting the container into a class (that is a service locator). Cycle detection is usually a design smell.
