  "â€‹Pleaseâ€‹ help",
  "Here is a base64 blob: " + "QUJDREVG".repeat(60),
]) {
  const v = g.aroundModelCall({ userText: t });
  console.log(" ", v.inputFlags.map((f) => f.code).join(",") || "clean", "|", v.userText.slice(0, 60).replace(/\n/g, " "));
}

console.log("\n== output ==");
const sources = ["Refunds are available within 30 days of purchase."];
for (const out of [
  "Refunds are available within 30 days [1].",
  "Refunds take 45 days [1].",
  "Refunds take 45 days [9].",
  "You can reach support at dana@acme.com or 555-123-4567 [1].",
  "<!-- session-marker-abc --> leaked",

}

console.log("\n== html ==");

console.log("\n== actions ==");

console.log(" search (ok):", JSON.stringify(g.beforeToolCall(caller, "search_orders", { query: "socks" }, {})));

```

**Run it.** `node guardrails.mjs` â†’ note that the unsupported-number check blocks "45 days" because 45
is not in the cited source, the unresolved-citation check blocks `[9]`, the canary catches a prompt leak,
and the bypass itself is written to the audit log.

**What to notice.**
- The input plane *quotes* a single-hit injection rather than blocking, so legitimate security questions
  still work; two hits block.
- The output plane's deterministic grounding check (numbers must appear in the cited source) catches a
  whole class of hallucination for free, before any judge call.
- Unknown tools default to `irreversible` â€” deny by default.
- Approval is bound to an argument hash, so arguments cannot change between proposal and approval.
- The bypass exists, is necessary, and is audited. A guardrail you cannot disable is an outage waiting
  to happen.

**Trade-offs.** Regex injection detection is trivially evaded and is not a security boundary; the real
boundaries are structural (least-privilege tools, tenant-scoped queries, no ambient credentials). The
deterministic grounding check is high-precision and will occasionally block a legitimate paraphrase that
reorders a number â€” hence the audit and the bypass.

## Problem 8 â€” A Cost-Tracking Wrapper

**Difficulty:** ðŸŸ¡ Intermediate Â· **Must-know**

**Spec.** A wrapper around every model call that: prices the call from config, attributes it to
feature/tenant/user, enforces per-tenant and global budgets, records cached vs. fresh tokens, tracks cost
per successful outcome, and emits the metrics a dashboard and an alert need.

```ts
// cost-tracker.mjs
// ============================================================ 1. PRICING IN CONFIG (never in logic)
const PRICING = {
  "model-a": { inputPerMTok: 3.00, outputPerMTok: 15.00, cachedInputPerMTok: 0.30, cacheWritePerMTok: 3.75 },
  "model-b": { inputPerMTok: 0.25, outputPerMTok: 1.25, cachedInputPerMTok: 0.025 },
  "model-embed": { inputPerMTok: 0.02, outputPerMTok: 0 },
  "model-rerank": { inputPerMTok: 0.10, outputPerMTok: 0 },
  "model-judge": { inputPerMTok: 1.00, outputPerMTok: 5.00, cachedInputPerMTok: 0.10 },
};
const M = 1_000_000;

// ============================================================ 2. LEDGER
export class Ledger {
  constructor() { this.records = []; this.budgets = new Map(); this.globalCap = Infinity; this.killSwitch = false; }

  setBudget(tenantId, { dailyCents, capModel }) {
    this.budgets.set(tenantId, { dailyCents, capModel, spentCents: 0, spentTokens: 0 });
  }
  setGlobalCap(cents) { this.globalCap = cents; }
  get globalSpent() { return this.records.reduce((s, r) => s + r.costCents, 0); }

  check(tenantId, estimateCents) {
    if (this.killSwitch) throw new BudgetError("kill_switch_on");
    const g = this.globalSpent;
    if (g + estimateCents > this.globalCap) throw new BudgetError("global_cap");
    const b = this.budgets.get(tenantId);
    if (b && b.spentCents + estimateCents > b.dailyCents) throw new BudgetError("tenant_daily_cap");
    return true;
  }

  record(r) { this.records.push(r);
    const b = this.budgets.get(r.tenantId);
    if (b) { b.spentCents += r.costCents; b.spentTokens += r.usage.inputTokens + r.usage.outputTokens; } }

  // Headline metric: cost per *successful outcome*, not per call.
  report() {
    const byFeature = new Map();
    for (const r of this.records) {
      const cur = byFeature.get(r.feature) ?? { calls: 0, okCalls: 0, cents: 0, tokens: 0,
        cachedTokens: 0, aborted: 0, retries: 0, byModel: {}, byComponent: {} };
      cur.calls++; cur.cents += r.costCents;
      cur.tokens += r.usage.inputTokens + r.usage.outputTokens;
      cur.cachedTokens += r.usage.cachedInputTokens;
      if (r.success) cur.okCalls++;
      if (r.aborted) cur.aborted++;
      if (r.attempt > 1) cur.retries++;
      cur.byModel[r.model] = (cur.byModel[r.model] ?? 0) + r.costCents;
      cur.byComponent[r.component] = (cur.byComponent[r.component] ?? 0) + r.costCents;
      byFeature.set(r.feature, cur);
    }
    return [...byFeature].map(([feature, v]) => ({
      feature, ...v,
      cacheHitRate: v.tokens ? v.cachedTokens / (v.tokens + v.cachedTokens) : 0,
      avgCentsPerCall: v.cents / v.calls,
      costPerSuccessCents: v.okCalls ? v.cents / v.okCalls : null,   // null, not Infinity: no data
      wasteRatio: (v.aborted + v.retries) / v.calls,
    }));
  }
}
class BudgetError extends Error { constructor(code) { super("budget: " + code); this.code = code; } }

// ============================================================ 3. WRAPPER
export function trackedClient({ ledger, client, component = "generation", onMetric }) {
  return async function call(req, ctx) {
    const pricing = PRICING[req.model];
    if (!pricing) throw new Error("no pricing configured for " + req.model);

    // Pre-flight estimate so we can refuse before spending.
    const estInput = estimateTokens(req.messages);
    const estOutput = req.maxOutputTokens ?? 400;
    const estimate = estimateCostCents({ inputTokens: estInput, outputTokens: estOutput, cachedInputTokens: 0 }, pricing, component);
    try { ledger.check(ctx.tenantId, estimate * 1.5); }
    catch (e) { onMetric?.("budget_blocked", { code: e.code, feature: ctx.feature }); throw e; }

    const t0 = performance.now();
    const started = Date.now();
    let res, aborted = false;
    try {
      res = await client(req, ctx);
    } catch (e) {
      aborted = e.name === "AbortError";
      ledger.record({ ...ctx, component, model: req.model, usage: zero(), costCents: 0,
        success: false, aborted, latencyMs: Date.now() - started, promptId: req.promptId,
        recipeId: req.recipeId, attempt: ctx.attempt ?? 1, at: started });
      throw e;
    }

    const cost = estimateCostCents(res.usage, pricing, component);
    const record = {
      ...ctx, component, model: req.model, usage: res.usage, costCents: cost.cents,
      breakdown: cost.breakdown,
      success: res.stopReason !== "error", aborted, cacheHit: res.usage.cachedInputTokens > 0,
      latencyMs: Date.now() - started, ttftMs: res.ttftMs ?? null,
      outputTruncated: res.stopReason === "max_tokens",
      promptId: req.promptId, recipeId: req.recipeId, attempt: ctx.attempt ?? 1,
      stopReason: res.stopReason, at: started,
    };
    ledger.record(record);

    for (const [m, v] of Object.entries({
      calls: 1, cost_cents: cost.cents, input_tokens: res.usage.inputTokens,
      output_tokens: res.usage.outputTokens, cached_tokens: res.usage.cachedInputTokens,
      latency_ms: record.latencyMs, ttft_ms: record.ttftMs ?? 0,
      truncated: record.outputTruncated ? 1 : 0, aborted: aborted ? 1 : 0,
    })) onMetric?.(m, { ...v, feature: ctx.feature, tenant: ctx.tenantId, model: req.model });

    return res;
  };
}

function estimateCostCents(usage, p, component) {
  const rates = component === "generation"
    ? [p.inputPerMTok, p.outputPerMTok, p.cachedInputPerMTok ?? p.inputPerMTok, p.cacheWritePerMTok ?? 0]
    : component === "embed" ? [p.inputPerMTok, 0, 0, 0]
    : [p.inputPerMTok, p.outputPerMTok, p.cachedInputPerMTok ?? p.inputPerMTok, 0];
  const fresh = Math.max(0, usage.inputTokens - usage.cachedInputTokens);
  const breakdown = {
    input: +(fresh / M * rates[0]).toFixed(6),
    output: +(usage.outputTokens / M * rates[1]).toFixed(6),
    cacheRead: +(usage.cachedInputTokens / M * rates[2]).toFixed(6),
  };
  return { cents: +(breakdown.input + breakdown.output + breakdown.cacheRead).toFixed(6), breakdown };
}
const estimateTokens = (arr) => Math.ceil(JSON.stringify(arr).length / 4);
const zero = () => ({ inputTokens: 0, outputTokens: 0, cachedInputTokens: 0 });

// ============================================================ 4. DEGRADATION: budgets route down a tier
export function budgetAwareRoute(ledger, { feature, tenantId }, candidates) {
  for (const cand of candidates) {
    try { ledger.check(tenantId, cand.estimateCents); return cand; }
    catch (e) { if (e.code === "kill_switch_on") break; }
  }
  return null;   // caller falls back to a deterministic, non-model answer
}

// ============================================================ 5. DEMO
const ledger = new Ledger();
ledger.setGlobalCap(1.00);
ledger.setBudget("t1", { dailyCents: 0.40 });
ledger.setBudget("t2", { dailyCents: 0.05 });

const fakeClient = async (req) => {
  const inTok = estimateTokens(req.messages);
  const outTok = Math.min(req.maxOutputTokens ?? 100, 120);
  return { content: [{ type: "text", text: "x".repeat(outTok * 4) }], stopReason: "end_turn",
    usage: { inputTokens: inTok, outputTokens: outTok, cachedInputTokens: req.cachedPrefix ?? 0 },
    ttftMs: 180 };
};

const call = trackedClient({ ledger, client: fakeClient });

const messages = [
  { role: "system", content: "You are a helpful assistant." + " Context. ".repeat(400) },  // ~1.6k tokens
  { role: "user", content: "Explain the refund policy." },
];

for (let i = 0; i < 6; i++) {
  try {
    await call({ model: "model-a", messages, maxOutputTokens: 120, cachedPrefix: i < 3 ? 1500 : 0 },
      { tenantId: "t1", userId: "u1", feature: "support.reply", promptId: "support.v7", recipeId: "support.v7+model-a" });
  } catch (e) { console.log("blocked:", e.code, "at request", i + 1); break; }
}
try { await call({ model: "model-b", messages, maxOutputTokens: 60 },
  { tenantId: "t2", userId: "u9", feature: "triage", promptId: "triage.v3" }); }
catch (e) { console.log("t2 blocked:", e.code); }

console.log("\nreport:");
console.table(ledger.report().map((r) => ({
  feature: r.feature, calls: r.calls, cents: +r.cents.toFixed(4),
  cacheHitRate: +r.cacheHitRate.toFixed(3), costPerSuccess: r.costPerSuccessCents?.toFixed(4),
  wasteRatio: +r.wasteRatio.toFixed(2),
})));

console.log("global spent:", ledger.globalSpent.toFixed(4), "of cap 1.00");
ledger.killSwitch = true;
try { await call({ model: "model-b", messages }, { tenantId: "t1", feature: "support.reply" }); }
catch (e) { console.log("kill switch:", e.code); }
console.log("\nsample record:", JSON.stringify(ledger.records[0], null, 2).slice(0, 600));
```

**Run it.** `node cost-tracker.mjs` â†’ the tenant with the large budget spends freely, the small-budget
tenant is blocked, the kill switch stops everything, and the report shows cache hit rate and cost per
success per feature.

**What to notice.**
- Budgets are checked *before* the call with a 1.5x estimate, so you never start work you cannot pay for.
- Costs are recorded on failure and abort too, because those tokens were billed.
- `costPerSuccessCents` is `null` when there is no successful call, rather than `Infinity` â€” a
  meaningless number in a dashboard hides the real problem.
- `cacheHitRate` is per feature, so a prompt-layout regression that kills caching is visible immediately.
- Pricing is config. Nothing in the logic knows a dollar figure.

**Trade-offs.** Tracking everything costs a write per call; in a very high-QPS system, aggregate
in-process and flush periodically rather than writing per call. Pre-flight estimates will be wrong for
unusual requests, which is why the check is a soft gate with an escalation path rather than a hard one
at the database level.

## Problem 9 â€” A Chunking-and-Indexing Script

**Difficulty:** ðŸ”´ Advanced Â· **Must-know**

**Spec.** A production-shaped ingestion script: parse a document into a structure tree, chunk by
structure with parent-child relationships, compute content hashes for incremental reindexing, embed in
batches with a cache, write chunks and vectors to an index, soft-delete with vacuum, and emit an
ingestion report plus a reindex plan.

```ts
// ingest.mjs â€” structure-aware chunking + incremental indexing, with a flat in-memory index
// standing in for the vector store.
import { createHash } from "node:crypto";
const sha256 = (s) => createHash("sha256").update(s).digest("hex");

// ============================================================ 1. PARSE (structure-aware)
export function parseMarkdown(src, meta) {
  const lines = src.split("\n");
  const blocks = [];
  let heading = null, buf = [];
  const flush = () => { if (buf.length) { blocks.push({ type: "text", text: buf.join(" ").trim() }); buf = []; } };
  for (const line of lines) {
    const h = line.match(/^(#{1,6})\s+(.*)$/);
    if (h) { flush(); heading = { level: h[1].length, text: h[2].trim() };
             blocks.push({ type: "heading", level: h[1].length, text: h[2].trim() }); }
    else if (/^\s*[-*]\s+/.test(line) || /^\s*\d+[.)]\s+/.test(line)) { flush();
             blocks.push({ type: "text", text: line.trim() }); }
    else if (/^\|.*\|$/.test(line)) { flush(); blocks.push({ type: "table", text: line.trim() }); }
    else if (line.trim() === "") flush();
    else buf.push(line.trim());
  }
  flush();
  return { ...meta, blocks, headings: blocks.filter((b) => b.type === "heading") };
}

// Merge consecutive table rows and always carry the header: a row without its header is meaningless.
function normalizeBlocks(blocks) {
  const out = [];
  let header = null;
  for (const b of blocks) {
    if (b.type !== "table") { out.push(b); continue; }
    const cells = b.text.split("|").slice(1, -1).map((c) => c.trim());
    if (!header) { header = cells; out.push({ ...b, kind: "table_header" }); }
    else out.push({ type: "text", text: `Table row â€” ${header.join(" | ")} :: ${cells.join(" | ")}` });
  }
  return out;
}

// ============================================================ 2. CHUNK: parent-child, breadcrumb prefix
const CHUNKER = { version: "struct-v4", targetWords: 140, maxWords: 220, minWords: 25, headingContext: 2 };

export function chunkDocument(doc) {
  const blocks = normalizeBlocks(doc.blocks);
  const leaves = [];
  const sections = [];
  let currentSection = null;
  let buf = [];

  const sectionId = (h) => `${doc.id}#${"h".repeat(h.level)}-${slug(h.text)}`;

  const flushSection = () => {
    if (!currentSection) return;
    const sectionText = buf.map((b) => b.text).join(" ");
    currentSection.text = `${doc.title} â€º ${currentSection.heading}\n\n${sectionText}`;
    currentSection.contentHash = sha256(sectionText);
    sections.push(currentSection);
    buf = [];
  };

  for (const b of blocks) {
    if (b.type === "heading") {
      flushSection();
      const stack = sections.filter((s) => s.level < b.level).map((s) => s.heading);
      currentSection = { id: sectionId(b), docId: doc.id, level: b.level, heading: b.text,
        breadcrumb: [...stack, b.text].join(" â€º "), title: doc.title,
        url: doc.url, updatedAt: doc.updatedAt, embeddable: false };
      continue;
    }
    if (!currentSection) {
      currentSection = { id: sectionId({ level: 1, text: "Overview" }), docId: doc.id, level: 1,
        heading: "Overview", breadcrumb: "Overview", title: doc.title, url: doc.url,
        updatedAt: doc.updatedAt, embeddable: false };
    }
    buf.push(b);
  }
  flushSection();

  // Leaves: paragraph-level within each section, grouped to the target size with a hard cap.
  for (const s of sections) {
    const paras = s.text.split("\n\n").slice(1).flatMap((p) => p.split(/(?<=\.)\s+/)).filter((p) => p.trim().length > 0);
    let group = [], words = 0;
    const emit = () => {
      if (group.length === 0) return;
      const body = group.join(" ").trim();
      if (words >= CHUNKER.minWords || group.length > 1) {
        leaves.push({
          id: `${s.id}~${leaves.length}`, parentId: s.id, docId: doc.id, sectionId: s.id,
          // Breadcrumb prefix: the embedding no longer represents an orphan fragment.
          text: `${doc.title} â€º ${s.breadcrumb}\n\n${body}`,
          body, wordCount: words, embeddable: true,
          title: doc.title, url: doc.url, heading: s.heading, updatedAt: doc.updatedAt,
          textHash: sha256(body),
        });
      }
      group = []; words = 0;
    };
    for (const p of paras) {
      const w = p.split(/\s+/).length;
      if (words + w > CHUNKER.maxWords) emit();
      group.push(p); words += w;
      if (words >= CHUNKER.targetWords) emit();
    }
    emit();
  }
  return { sections, leaves };
}
const slug = (s) => s.toLowerCase().replace(/[^a-z0-9]+/g, "-").replace(/^-|-$/g, "").slice(0, 48);

// ============================================================ 3. EMBED with a content-hash cache
const DIM = 128;
function embed(text) {
  const v = new Float32Array(DIM);
  for (const t of text.toLowerCase().match(/[a-z0-9]+/g) ?? []) v[fnv(t) % DIM] += 1;
  let n = Math.hypot(...v) || 1;
  for (let i = 0; i < DIM; i++) v[i] /= n;
  return v;
}
function fnv(s) { let h = 2166136261; for (const c of s) { h ^= c.charCodeAt(0); h = Math.imul(h, 16777619); } return h >>> 0; }

class Embedder {
  constructor({ batchSize = 32, cache = new Map() } = {}) { this.batchSize = batchSize; this.cache = cache;
    this.stats = { embedded: 0, cacheHits: 0, batches: 0 }; }
  async embedAll(texts) {
    const out = new Array(texts.length);
    const todo = [];
    texts.forEach((t, i) => {
      const key = sha256(t);
      if (this.cache.has(key)) { out[i] = this.cache.get(key); this.stats.cacheHits++; }
      else todo.push({ i, key, text: t });
    });
    for (let b = 0; b < todo.length; b += this.batchSize) {
      const batch = todo.slice(b, b + this.batchSize);
      this.stats.batches++;
      // A real embedder is one network call per batch. Batch size is a cost/latency dial.
      await sleep(2);
      for (const item of batch) {
        const v = embed(item.text);
        this.cache.set(item.key, v);
        out[item.i] = v;
        this.stats.embedded++;
      }
    }
    return out;
  }
}
const sleep = (ms) => new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, ms));

// ============================================================ 4. INDEX with incremental reindex + tombstones
class ChunkStore {
  constructor() {
    this.sections = new Map(); this.leaves = new Map();
    this.embeddings = new Map();        // chunkId -> vector
    this.docs = new Map();              // docId -> { contentHash, indexedAt, chunkerVer, embedModel }
    this.tombstones = [];
  }
  async upsertDocument(doc, { embedder, chunkerVer, embedModel }) {
    const existing = this.docs.get(doc.id);
    const contentHash = sha256(doc.blocks.map((b) => b.text).join("|"));
    if (existing?.contentHash === contentHash && existing.chunkerVer === chunkerVer
        && existing.embedModel === embedModel) {
      return { docId: doc.id, action: "skipped", reason: "unchanged" };
    }

    const { sections, leaves } = chunkDocument(doc);

    // Reuse vectors for byte-identical chunks: the single biggest ingest cost saving.
    const byHash = new Map();
    for (const l of leaves) {
      const prevId = [...this.leaves.values()].find((p) => p.docId === l.docId && p.textHash === l.textHash);
      if (prevId && this.embeddings.has(prevId)) byHash.set(l.id, prevId);
    }
    const toEmbed = leaves.filter((l) => !byHash.has(l.id));
    const vectors = toEmbed.length ? await embedder.embedAll(toEmbed.map((l) => l.text)) : [];

    // Soft-delete the previous generation, then write the new one.
    const oldLeaves = [...this.leaves.values()].filter((l) => l.docId === doc.id).map((l) => l.id);
    const oldSections = [...this.sections.values()].filter((s) => s.docId === doc.id).map((s) => s.id);
    for (const id of oldLeaves) { this.leaves.delete(id); this.embeddings.delete(id);
      this.tombstones.push({ id, at: Date.now(), reason: "reindex" }); }
    for (const id of oldSections) this.sections.delete(id);

    for (const s of sections) this.sections.set(s.id, s);
    let vi = 0;
    for (const l of leaves) {
      this.leaves.set(l.id, l);
      this.embeddings.set(l.id, byHash.get(l.id) ? this.embeddings.get(byHash.get(l.id)) ?? embed(l.text) : vectors[vi++]);
    }
    this.docs.set(doc.id, { contentHash, indexedAt: Date.now(), chunkerVer, embedModel,
      leafCount: leaves.length, sectionCount: sections.length });
    return { docId: doc.id, action: existing ? "updated" : "inserted",
      sections: sections.length, leaves: leaves.length,
      embedded: toEmbed.length, reusedVectors: byHash.size,
      tombstoned: oldLeaves.length };
  }

  deleteDocument(docId, reason = "source_removed") {
    const n = [...this.leaves.keys()].filter((id) => this.leaves.get(id).docId === docId).length;
    for (const l of [...this.leaves.values()].filter((l) => l.docId === docId)) {
      this.leaves.delete(l.id); this.embeddings.delete(l.id);
      this.tombstones.push({ id: l.id, at: Date.now(), reason });
    }
    for (const s of [...this.sections.values()].filter((s) => s.docId === docId)) this.sections.delete(s.id);
    this.docs.delete(docId);
    return { docId, action: "deleted", leavesRemoved: n };
  }

  vacuum(maxAgeDays = 7, batch = 1000) {
    const cutoff = Date.now() - maxAgeDays * 86_400_000;
    const doomed = this.tombstones.filter((t) => t.at < cutoff).slice(0, batch);
    this.tombstones = this.tombstones.filter((t) => !doomed.includes(t));
    return { removed: doomed.length, remaining: this.tombstones.length };
  }

  search(qv, k, { tenantId } = {}) {
    const out = [];
    for (const [id, v] of this.embeddings) {
      const c = this.leaves.get(id);
      if (!c) continue;
      if (tenantId && !String(id).startsWith(tenantId + ":")) continue;
      out.push({ id, chunk: c, score: cos(qv, v) });
    }
    return out.sort((a, b) => b.score - a.score).slice(0, k);
  }

  // Reindex plan: what a model/chunker change would cost.
  reindexPlan({ chunkerVer, embedModel }) {
    const docs = [...this.docs.entries()];
    return {
      totalDocs: docs.length,
      needsRechunk: docs.filter(([, d]) => d.chunkerVer !== chunkerVer).length,
      needsReembed: docs.filter(([, d]) => d.embedModel !== embedModel).length,
      leafVectors: this.embeddings.size,
      tombstones: this.tombstones.length,
      estimatedEmbeddingCalls: docs.filter(([, d]) => d.embedModel !== embedModel)
        .reduce((s, [, d]) => s + d.leafCount, 0),
      strategy: "dual-index: write chunks_v2, shadow query, compare recall, cut over",
    };
  }

  stats() {
    return { docs: this.docs.size, sections: this.sections.size, leaves: this.leaves.size,
      vectors: this.embeddings.size, tombstones: this.tombstones.length,
      avgLeafWords: mean([...this.leaves.values()].map((l) => l.wordCount)).toFixed(1) };
  }
}
const cos = (a, b) => { let d = 0; for (let i = 0; i < a.length; i++) d += a[i] * b[i]; return d; };
const mean = (xs) => (xs.length ? xs.reduce((s, x) => s + x, 0) / xs.length : 0);

// ============================================================ 5. RUN IT

| Item class | Refundable | Window |
| Physical | Yes | 30 days |

## Process

const DOCS = [
  { id: "t1:refunds", tenantId: "t1", title: "Refund Policy", url: "/policies/refunds",
    updatedAt: "2026-04-01", blocks: parseMarkdown(REFUNDS, { id: "t1:refunds", tenantId: "t1",
      title: "Refund Policy", url: "/policies/refunds", updatedAt: "2026-04-01" }).blocks },
];

const store = new ChunkStore();
const embedder = new Embedder({ batchSize: 16 });

console.log("== first ingest ==");
console.log(store.upsertDocument(DOCS[0], { embedder, chunkerVer: CHUNKER.version, embedModel: "embed-a" }));
console.log("embedder stats:", embedder.stats);
console.log("store:", store.stats());

console.log("\n== sample leaves ==");
for (const l of [...store.leaves.values()].slice(0, 4)) {
  console.log(`  [${l.wordCount}w] ${l.id}\n    ${l.text.replace(/\n/g, " | ").slice(0, 110)}`);
}

console.log("\n== re-ingest unchanged ==");
console.log(store.upsertDocument(DOCS[0], { embedder, chunkerVer: CHUNKER.version, embedModel: "embed-a" }));

console.log("\n== re-ingest after an edit (one section changed) ==");
const edited = { ...DOCS[0], updatedAt: "2026-06-01",
  blocks: parseMarkdown(REFUNDS.replace("within 30 days of the original purchase date",
    "within 45 days of the original purchase date"), DOCS[0]).blocks };
console.log(store.upsertDocument(edited, { embedder, chunkerVer: CHUNKER.version, embedModel: "embed-a" }));

console.log("\n== delete propagation ==");
console.log(store.deleteDocument("t1:refunds", "policy_retired"));
console.log("search after delete returns:", store.search(embed("refund policy"), 5).length);

console.log("\n== vacuum ==");
console.log(store.vacuum(0, 10));

console.log("\n== reindex plan (chunker + embedding model change) ==");
console.log(store.reindexPlan({ chunkerVer: "struct-v5", embedModel: "embed-b" }));
```

**Run it.** `node ingest.mjs` â†’ observe: the unchanged re-ingest is skipped; the edited re-ingest reuses
vectors for untouched chunks; deletion propagates to leaves, embeddings, and sections; vacuum clears
tombstones; and the reindex plan quantifies what a model change would cost.

**What to notice.**
- The chunker records `chunkerVer` and `embedModel` per document, which is what makes
  "unchanged â†’ skip" and the reindex plan possible at all.
- Table rows carry the header row, so an extracted row is interpretable.
- Vector reuse by `textHash` is the difference between re-embedding 200 chunks and 3.
- Deletes are soft first (tombstone) and physical later (vacuum), so recent deletions stay debuggable.
- The reindex plan refuses to be a surprise: it names the strategy (dual-index) rather than implying an
  in-place rebuild.

**Trade-offs.** Parent-child retrieval costs storing both levels and resolving parents at query time, and
it slightly reduces the number of independently retrievable units. Breadcrumb prefixes cost tokens per
chunk and duplicate text, and they measurably improve retrieval. Both are worth it. Soft deletes cost
storage and index quality until vacuumed; hard deletes cost you the ability to debug "why did this come
up?"

## Problem 10 â€” A Human-in-the-Loop Approval Flow

**Difficulty:** ðŸ”´ Advanced Â· **Must-know**

**Spec.** A complete approval system: the model proposes, the *server* renders the confirmation (never
the model), the proposal is persisted with an argument hash and a TTL, approval is bound to those exact
arguments with an atomic claim, edits are supported, four-eyes and re-authentication are enforced, and
every decision is audited. Includes the reviewer's queue with SLA and expiry.

```ts
// hitl.mjs â€” runnable end to end, in-memory store, deterministic fake model.
import { randomUUID, createHash } from "node:crypto";
const sha256 = (s) => createHash("sha256").update(s).digest("hex");

// ============================================================ 1. DATA MODEL
const db = {
  proposals: new Map(),
  executions: new Map(),      // idempotencyKey -> result
  audit: [],
  appendAudit(e) { this.audit.push({ at: new Date().toISOString(), ...e }); },
};

// ============================================================ 2. RISK CLASSIFICATION (server-side policy)
const TOOL_POLICY = {
  search_orders:     { risk: "none",           scopes: ["orders:read"],           idempotent: true },
  draft_reply:       { risk: "reversible",     scopes: ["orders:write"],          idempotent: false },
  cancel_order:      { risk: "irreversible",   scopes: ["orders:write"],          idempotent: false },
  issue_refund:      { risk: "financial",      scopes: ["orders:write"],          idempotent: false },
  rotate_api_keys:   { risk: "security",       scopes: ["keys:write"],            idempotent: false },
  transfer_funds:    { risk: "financial",      scopes: ["payments:write"],        idempotent: false },
};

export function classifyRisk(tool, args) {
  const p = TOOL_POLICY[tool];
  if (!p) return { level: "irreversible", blastRadius: Infinity, requiresReauth: true,
                   requiresMfa: true, requiresApproval: true, unknownTool: true };
  const count = Array.isArray(args?.orderIds) ? args.orderIds.length : args?.all ? Infinity : 1;
  const amount = typeof args?.amountCents === "number" ? args.amountCents : 0;
  return {
    level: p.risk,
    blastRadius: count,
    amountCents: amount,
    requiresApproval: p.risk !== "none" && p.risk !== "reversible",
    requiresReauth: p.risk === "financial" || p.risk === "security",
    requiresMfa: p.risk === "security",
  };
}

// ============================================================ 3. CONFIRMATION RENDERED BY THE SERVER
// The model never authors confirmation copy. Templates + validated args only, so a prompt-injected
// model cannot talk a human into approving something else.
const CONFIRMATIONS = {
  transfer_funds: (a) => ({
    kind: "financial", title: "Confirm transfer",
    lines: [`Amount: ${money(a.amountCents, a.currency)}`,
            `To: ${maskAcct(a.destinationAccount)}`, `From: ${maskAcct(a.sourceAccount)}`,
            `Memo: ${a.memo ?? "(none)"}`],
    confirmLabel: `Transfer ${money(a.amountCents, a.currency)}`, destructive: true,
    requiresTyping: a.amountCents > 100_000 ? String(a.amountCents / 100) : null,
  }),
  issue_refund: (a) => ({
    kind: "financial", title: "Confirm refund",
    lines: [`Order: ${a.orderId}`, `Amount: ${money(a.amountCents, a.currency)}`,
            `Reason: ${a.reason}`, "Funds return to the original payment method within 5 business days."],
    confirmLabel: "Issue refund", destructive: true,
  }),
  cancel_order: (a) => ({
    kind: "destructive", title: "Confirm cancellation",
    lines: [`Order: ${a.orderId}`, `Items: ${a.itemCount ?? "?"}`,
            "This cannot be undone and stock is released."],
    confirmLabel: "Cancel order", destructive: true,
  }),
  rotate_api_keys: (a) => ({
    kind: "security", title: "Confirm key rotation",
    lines: [`Environment: ${a.environment}`, "All existing keys stop working immediately.",
            "Every integration using a rotated key will begin failing."],
    confirmLabel: "Rotate keys", destructive: true,
  }),
  draft_reply: (a) => ({
    kind: "reversible", title: "Review drafted reply",
    lines: [`To: ${a.ticketId}`, "This draft will be visible to the customer."],
    confirmLabel: "Send draft", destructive: false,
  }),
};

function renderConfirmation(tool, args) {
  const f = CONFIRMATIONS[tool];
  if (f) return f(args);
  return { kind: "generic", title: `Confirm ${humanize(tool)}`,
           lines: Object.entries(args).map(([k, v]) => `${k}: ${JSON.stringify(v)}`),
           confirmLabel: "Yes, do it", destructive: true };
}
const money = (cents, cur = "USD") => new Intl.NumberFormat("en-US",
  { style: "currency", currency: cur }).format((cents ?? 0) / 100);
const maskAcct = (a) => a ? "â€¢â€¢â€¢â€¢" + String(a).slice(-4) : "(none)";
const humanize = (s) => s.replace(/_/g, " ");

// ============================================================ 4. PROPOSAL LIFECYCLE
export function propose({ conversationId, runId, tool, args, caller }) {
  const policy = TOOL_POLICY[tool];
  if (!policy) return { ok: false, code: "unknown_tool" };

  // Authorization happens here, at proposal time, and again at execution time.
  const missing = policy.scopes.filter((s) => !caller.scopes.has(s));
  if (missing.length) {
    db.appendAudit({ event: "proposal_denied", tool, by: caller.userId, reason: "missing_scope", missing });
    return { ok: false, code: "missing_scope", missing };
  }

  const risk = classifyRisk(tool, args);
  const proposal = {
    id: randomUUID(), conversationId, runId, tool, args, risk,
    proposedBy: caller.userId, tenantId: caller.tenantId,
    confirmation: renderConfirmation(tool, args),
    argsHash: sha256(canonical(args)),          // approval binds to these exact arguments
    status: risk.requiresApproval ? "pending" : "auto",
    createdAt: Date.now(),
    expiresAt: Date.now() + 10 * 60_000,
    slaDueAt: Date.now() + (risk.level === "security" ? 30 : risk.level === "financial" ? 60 : 1440) * 60_000,
    reviewerId: null, decisionReason: null, edits: null,
  };
  db.proposals.set(proposal.id, proposal);
  db.appendAudit({ event: "proposal_created", id: proposal.id, tool, by: caller.userId, risk: risk.level,
                   blastRadius: risk.blastRadius, amountCents: risk.amountCents ?? 0 });
  return { ok: true, proposal };
}

export function resolve(proposalId, reviewer, decision, edits = {}) {
  const p = db.proposals.get(proposalId);
  if (!p) return { ok: false, code: "not_found" };
  if (p.status !== "pending") return { ok: false, code: "already_" + p.status };

  if (Date.now() > p.expiresAt) {
    p.status = "expired";
    db.appendAudit({ event: "proposal_expired", id: p.id, tool: p.tool });
    return { ok: false, code: "expired" };
  }
  if (p.tenantId !== reviewer.tenantId) return { ok: false, code: "wrong_tenant" };
  // Four-eyes: the proposer cannot approve their own high-risk action.
  if (p.risk.requiresReauth && p.proposedBy === reviewer.userId) {
    db.appendAudit({ event: "approval_blocked_four_eyes", id: p.id, tool: p.tool, reviewer: reviewer.userId });
    return { ok: false, code: "four_eyes_required" };
  }
  if (p.risk.requiresReauth && Date.now() - (reviewer.lastAuthAt ?? 0) > 5 * 60_000) {
    return { ok: false, code: "reauth_required" };
  }
  if (p.risk.requiresMfa && !reviewer.mfaVerified) return { ok: false, code: "mfa_required" };

  // Edits are allowed, but they change the hash, so they invalidate the earlier confirmation.
  const finalArgs = edits.args ? { ...p.args, ...edits.args } : p.args;
  const finalHash = sha256(canonical(finalArgs));
  if (finalHash !== p.argsHash) {
    return { ok: false, code: "arguments_changed",
             detail: "edits change the arguments; re-confirm with the new values" };
  }

  // Atomic claim: two concurrent approvals cannot both execute.
  if (p.status !== "pending") return { ok: false, code: "already_" + p.status };
  p.status = "executing";
  p.reviewerId = reviewer.userId;
  p.decisionReason = edits.reason ?? null;
  p.resolvedAt = Date.now();

  let result;
  try {
    result = execute(p, finalArgs, reviewer);
  } catch (e) {
    p.status = "failed";
    db.appendAudit({ event: "execution_failed", id: p.id, tool: p.tool, error: String(e.message) });
    return { ok: false, code: "execution_failed", detail: String(e.message) };
  }

  p.status = decision === "reject" ? "rejected" : decision === "edit" ? "edited" : "approved";
  db.appendAudit({ event: "approval_" + p.status, id: p.id, tool: p.tool,
                   reviewer: reviewer.userId, by: p.proposedBy, risk: p.risk.level,
                   amountCents: p.risk.amountCents ?? 0, reason: p.decisionReason });
  return { ok: true, proposal: p, result };
}

function execute(p, args, caller) {
  // Idempotency: resuming a run or double-clicking cannot duplicate a side effect.
  const key = `${p.tool}:${p.argsHash}`;
  if (db.executions.has(key)) return { ...db.executions.get(key), deduplicated: true };
  let result;
  switch (p.tool) {
    case "transfer_funds": result = { transferId: "TR-" + randomUUID().slice(0, 8), ...args, status: "settling" }; break;
    case "issue_refund":   result = { refundId: "RF-" + randomUUID().slice(0, 8), ...args, status: "approved" }; break;
    case "cancel_order":   result = { orderId: args.orderId, status: "cancelled" }; break;
    case "rotate_api_keys":result = { environment: args.environment, rotatedKeys: 3, status: "rotated" }; break;
    case "draft_reply":    result = { ticketId: args.ticketId, sent: true }; break;
    default: throw new Error("no executor for " + p.tool);
  }
  db.executions.set(key, result);
  void caller;
  return result;
}

// Rejection feeds a structured reason back so the next attempt is informed, not a repeat.
export function rejectionFeedback(p) {
  return `A human reviewer rejected the proposed ${p.tool} action. ` +
         `Reason: ${p.decisionReason ?? "not supplied"}. Do not retry the same action unchanged. ` +
         `Either propose a materially different action or ask the user for what they want.`;
}

// ============================================================ 5. QUEUE with SLA and escalation
export function reviewQueue({ reviewer, limit = 20 } = {}) {
  const now = Date.now();
  const all = [...db.proposals.values()].filter((p) => p.status === "pending" && p.tenantId === reviewer.tenantId);
  const scored = all.map((p) => {
    const overdue = now > p.slaDueAt;
    const expiringSoon = p.expiresAt - now < 120_000;
    const priority = p.risk.level === "security" ? 0 : p.risk.level === "financial" ? 1
      : (p.risk.blastRadius === Infinity ? 0 : p.risk.blastRadius > 10 ? 1 : 2);
    return { p, overdue, expiringSoon, priority };
  });
  return scored
    .sort((a, b) => a.priority - b.priority || Number(b.overdue) - Number(a.overdue)
                  || a.p.slaDueAt - b.p.slaDueAt)
    .slice(0, limit)
    .map(({ p, overdue, expiringSoon }) => ({
      id: p.id, tool: p.tool, confirmation: p.confirmation, risk: p.risk,
      proposedBy: p.proposedBy, rationale: p.rationale ?? null,
      slaDueAt: new Date(p.slaDueAt).toISOString(),
      expiresAt: new Date(p.expiresAt).toISOString(), overdue, expiringSoon,
      canSelfApprove: !(p.risk.requiresReauth && p.proposedBy === reviewer.userId),
    }));
}

// Progressive autonomy: relax approval requirements per tool as measured intervention rates drop.
export function maybeAutoApprove(tool, risk, tenant, stats) {
  const s = stats[tenant]?.[tool];
  if (!s || s.reviews < 50) return false;                 // not enough evidence
  if (s.interventionRate > 0.05) return false;            // humans are intervening; keep asking
  if (s.escalationRate > 0.01) return false;
  if (risk.level === "security") return false;            // never auto-approve security actions
  if (risk.level === "financial" && risk.amountCents > 10_000) return false;
  return true;
}

// ============================================================ 6. THE MODEL SIDE
// The model emits tool calls; the orchestrator decides. The model has no approval pathway.
async function fakeModel() {
  return { toolCalls: [
    { name: "search_orders", args: { query: "wool socks" } },
    { name: "transfer_funds", args: { amountCents: 25_000, currency: "USD",
      sourceAccount: "acct_8812", destinationAccount: "acct_4417", memo: "supplier payout" } },
  ]};
}

export async function runWithApproval({ caller, reviewer }) {
  const res = await fakeModel();
  const out = [];
  for (const call of res.toolCalls) {
    const risk = classifyRisk(call.name, call.args);
    const pr = propose({ conversationId: "c1", tool: call.name, args: call.args, caller });
    if (!pr.ok) { out.push({ tool: call.name, result: pr }); continue; }
    if (pr.proposal.status === "auto") {
      out.push({ tool: call.name, result: { ok: true, auto: true,
        value: execute(pr.proposal, pr.proposal.args, caller) } });
      continue;
    }
    out.push({ tool: call.name, awaiting: pr.proposal.id, confirmation: pr.proposal.confirmation,
      risk, argsHash: pr.proposal.argsHash.slice(0, 12) });
    out.push({ _pending: pr.proposal });
  }
  return { out, reviewer, resolve: (id, decision, edits) => resolve(id, reviewer, decision, edits) };
}

// ============================================================ 7. DEMO
const alice = { userId: "alice", tenantId: "t1", scopes: new Set(["orders:read", "payments:write"]),
                lastAuthAt: Date.now(), mfaVerified: true };
const bob   = { userId: "bob",   tenantId: "t1", scopes: new Set(["orders:read", "orders:write"]),
                lastAuthAt: Date.now(), mfaVerified: false };
const carol = { userId: "carol", tenantId: "t2", scopes: new Set(["orders:read", "keys:write"]),
                lastAuthAt: Date.now(), mfaVerified: true };

const run = await runWithApproval({ caller: alice, reviewer: bob });
const transfer = run.out.find((o) => o.awaiting);
console.log("== proposal awaiting review ==");
console.log(JSON.stringify({ tool: transfer.tool, confirmation: transfer.confirmation,
  risk: transfer.risk, argsHash: transfer.argsHash }, null, 2));

console.log("\n== reviewer's queue ==");
console.table(reviewQueue({ reviewer: bob }));

console.log("\n== rejections that must be refused ==");
console.log(" alice self-approves:", JSON.stringify(run.resolve(transfer.awaiting, alice, "approve")));
console.log(" carol (other tenant):", JSON.stringify(run.resolve(transfer.awaiting, carol, "approve")));
console.log(" stale auth (bob):", JSON.stringify(run.resolve(transfer.awaiting,
  { ...bob, lastAuthAt: Date.now() - 10 * 60_000 }, "approve")));
console.log(" attempt to change the amount:", JSON.stringify(run.resolve(transfer.awaiting, bob, "edit",
  { args: { amountCents: 250_000 }, reason: "correcting the amount" })));

console.log("\n== bob approves the real thing ==");
const approved = run.resolve(transfer.awaiting, bob, "approve");
console.log(JSON.stringify({ ok: approved.ok, status: approved.proposal?.status,
  result: approved.result }, null, 2));

console.log("\n== idempotency: replaying execution ==");
console.log(JSON.stringify(execute(db.proposals.get(transfer.awaiting), db.proposals.get(transfer.awaiting).args, bob)));

console.log("\n== rejection path feeds back a reason ==");
const d = propose({ conversationId: "c1", tool: "issue_refund", caller: bob,
  args: { orderId: "ORD-9", amountCents: 5000, currency: "USD", reason: "duplicate charge" } });
const rej = run.resolve(d.proposal.id, bob, "reject", { reason: "order was already refunded via the returns desk" });
console.log("status:", rej.proposal.status, "| feedback:", rejectionFeedback(rej.proposal).slice(0, 120));

console.log("\n== expiry ==");
const e = propose({ conversationId: "c1", tool: "cancel_order", caller: bob, args: { orderId: "ORD-3", itemCount: 2 } });
db.proposals.get(e.proposal.id).expiresAt = Date.now() - 1;
console.log(JSON.stringify(run.resolve(e.proposal.id, bob, "approve")));

console.log("\n== audit trail ==");
console.table(db.audit.map((a) => ({ event: a.event, tool: a.tool ?? "", by: a.by ?? a.reviewer ?? "" })));
```

**Run it.** `node hitl.mjs` â†’ observe the four refusals (self-approval, wrong tenant, stale auth,
argument tampering) all failing for *structural* reasons, then the correct approval executing exactly the
proposed action, then idempotent replay, then the rejection feedback, then expiry.

**What to notice.**
- Confirmation copy comes from server-side templates over validated arguments. A prompt-injected model
  cannot change what the reviewer is shown.
- `argsHash` makes approval binding: any edit to the arguments invalidates the confirmation and forces a
  fresh approval.
- Four-eyes is enforced for financial and security actions, plus re-auth within 5 minutes and MFA for
  security actions.
- The status transition to `executing` happens before execution, and execution is keyed by
  `tool:argsHash`, so double-clicks and resumed runs deduplicate.
- Rejections produce structured feedback so the model changes approach instead of retrying.
- Expired proposals fail closed.
- Auto-approval is gated on measured intervention rate and never applies to security actions.

**Trade-offs.** HITL converts latency you control into latency you do not, and creates a queue with its
own SLAs and a rubber-stamping risk. Measure intervention rate (edited-or-rejected Ã· total) as the real
safety metric: near zero on high-risk actions means your reviewers are not reading, and your control is
theatre. Progressive autonomy is the way out â€” start conservative, then relax per tool per tenant as
evidence accumulates.

---

---
# PHASE 13 DEBUGGING SCENARIOS (12)

> Each scenario is a realistic production failure, presented as: symptom â†’ how to diagnose â†’ root cause
> â†’ fix. Several are deliberately subtle.

---

## Scenario 1 â€” The Chat UI froze after a deploy

ðŸŸ¡ Intermediate Â· **Must-know**

**Symptom.** Streaming chat worked in staging. In production, users click send and the full response
appears at once after a long pause. Locally it streams correctly.

**Diagnosis.** Compare response headers between environments.

```
local:      content-type: text/event-stream
production: content-type: text/event-stream
```

Headers match, so it is not the app. Check *when* the first byte arrives:

```bash
curl -N -s -X POST https://prod/api/chat -d '{"conversationId":"c1","text":"hi"}' \
  -w '\nTTFB=%{time_starttransfer} TOTAL=%{time_total}\n'
```

TTFB â‰ˆ total time. So the server is not emitting early. Two candidates: (a) a reverse proxy is
buffering, (b) the server is not actually streaming.

**Instrument.**

```ts
const t0 = Date.now();
const res = await client.stream(req);
console.log("first provider event after", Date.now() - t0, "ms");
res.on("delta", () => { if (!firstSentAt) { firstSentAt = Date.now(); console.log("first byte to client", firstSentAt - t0, "ms"); } });
```

The first provider event arrives at 40ms but the first byte to the client arrives at 2.8s â€” the delay is
*after* your handler.

**Root cause.** Nginx (or an ingress) buffers the upstream response. `proxy_buffering on` with a
buffer size larger than your response accumulates the whole stream before forwarding.

**Fix.**

```nginx
location /api/chat {
  proxy_pass http://app;
  proxy_http_version 1.1;
  proxy_set_header Connection '';
  proxy_buffering off;              # do not buffer SSE
  proxy_cache off;
  chunked_transfer_encoding on;
  proxy_read_timeout 300s;
  gzip off;                          # gzip re-buffers
}
```

Plus the response headers from 13.2.5: `cache-control: no-cache, no-transform`,
`x-accel-buffering: no`. The `no-transform` directive also stops intermediate proxies transforming the
stream.

**Lesson.** Streaming is a property of the whole path, not just your handler. Add a CI smoke test that
asserts first-byte latency is well under total latency, or this will regress silently.

---

## Scenario 2 â€” Costs tripled overnight with no traffic increase

ðŸ”´ Advanced Â· **Must-know**

**Symptom.** Daily spend went from $180 to $540. Request volume flat. No deploy on the model side.

**Diagnosis.** Group the ledger by dimension.

```sql
SELECT date_trunc('hour', at) h, model, feature, count(*) calls,
       sum(input_tokens) in_tok, sum(cached_tokens) cached, sum(output_tokens) out_tok,
       round(sum(cost_cents),2) cents
  FROM spend_records
 WHERE at > now() - interval '3 days'
 GROUP BY 1,2,3 ORDER BY 1 DESC, 6 DESC LIMIT 20;
```

Two findings: `cached_tokens` dropped to near zero for `support.reply`, and `output_tokens` per call rose
~2.5x.

**Investigate the cache collapse first.** A `cacheHitRate` dashboard shows a step change at 03:00 UTC.

```ts
// Diff the rendered prefix between a hit and a miss.
const a = renderSupportPrompt(fixedInput);
const b = renderSupportPrompt(fixedInput);
console.log(cachePrefixHash(a.messages), cachePrefixHash(b.messages));   // differ!
console.log(JSON.stringify(a.messages[0]).slice(0, 200));
console.log(JSON.stringify(b.messages[0]).slice(0, 200));
```

The system prompt now starts with a tenant name â€” a personalization change shipped at 03:00. The prefix
is no longer stable across requests, so nothing caches.

**Root cause (two bugs).**
1. **Personalization moved into the system prompt**, which sits in the cached prefix. The user's name
   must go in the tail.
2. **Output growth**: the prompt edit also added "provide a thorough, detailed response" while a separate
   change added three more few-shot examples. Output tokens rose accordingly.

**Fix.**
- Move identity into the volatile region; keep system + tools static.
- Add the CI assertion from 13.3.4: `expect(cachePrefixHash(render(fixedInput))).toEqual(CACHE_PREFIX_HASH)`.
  This would have caught it before deploy.
- Revert the verbosity instruction; set `maxOutputTokens` per feature rather than relying on prose.

**Lesson.** Cost regressions are usually prompt-layout regressions. Track cache hit rate as a first-class
SLO per feature, and snapshot-test the prefix hash.

---

## Scenario 3 â€” Truncated JSON crashes the parser

ðŸŸ¡ Intermediate Â· **Must-know**

**Symptom.** ~4% of extraction requests fail with `Unexpected end of JSON input`. The failure rate is
higher on long documents.

**Diagnosis.** Look at the failed requests' `stop_reason`.

```sql
SELECT stop_reason, count(*), round(avg(output_tokens))
  FROM message_observations
 WHERE created_at > now() - interval '1 day' AND output_schema_ok = false
 GROUP BY 1;
```

100% of failures are `max_tokens`. Not a parser bug. The response is being cut mid-object because the
output budget is smaller than the schema requires.

The schema has 14 fields, several with `maxLength: 2000`, and `maxOutputTokens` is 1,200. A maximal
answer needs well over 4,000 tokens.

**Root cause.** The output budget was set for the old 6-field schema and never revisited.

**Fix â€” in order of preference.**

1. **Raise the budget from the schema**, with headroom measured from the observed distribution:

```ts
const required = estimateMaxTokensFromSchema(schema);       // sum of maxLengths + overhead
const budget = Math.ceil(required * 1.15);
// and derive the actual max from p99 of observed output, not a guess:
const p99 = percentile(outputTokensByFeature, 0.99);
const maxOutputTokens = Math.max(budget, p99 * 1.3);
```

2. **Detect it and fail loudly**, not with a parse error:

```ts
if (res.stopReason === "max_tokens") {
  metrics.count("truncation", { feature });
  throw new TruncationError({ feature, outputTokens: res.usage.outputTokens, required });
}
```

3. **Reduce what must be generated**: split the schema into a small "primary" object plus a detail array
   with a cap, so a complete answer always fits.

**Lesson.** `stop_reason` is the field that tells you the truth. Never detect truncation by string
heuristics, and never set `maxOutputTokens` without deriving it from something.

---

## Scenario 4 â€” RAG answers cite sources that do not contain the answer

ðŸ”´ Advanced Â· **Must-know**

**Symptom.** Users report "it made up a citation." The answer looks reasonable; the cited chunk is
topically related but does not contain the claim.

**Diagnosis.** Build a per-claim check over a sample.

```ts
const sample = await db.query(
  `SELECT id, content, citations FROM messages
    WHERE feature = 'rag.answer' AND status = 'complete' AND created_at > now() - interval '2 days'
    ORDER BY random() LIMIT 200`);
const sources = await loadSourcesFor(sample.rows);
const bad = [];
for (const m of sample.rows) {
  const cited = extractCitations(m.content);
  for (const n of cited) {
    const src = sources.get(m.id)?.[n - 1];
    if (!src) { bad.push({ id: m.id, why: "unresolved", n }); continue; }
    const claims = splitClaims(m.content).filter((c) => c.citations.includes(n));
    const support = judgeSupport(claims, src);
    if (support.unsupported > 0) bad.push({ id: m.id, why: "unsupported", n, support });
  }
}
console.log("bad citation rate:", bad.length / sample.rows.length);
```

Rate is 11%. Now check *which* source numbers are being cited.

```sql
SELECT (regexp_match(content, '\[(\d+)\]'))[1] AS cite, count(*)
  FROM messages WHERE feature='rag.answer' AND created_at > now() - interval '2 days'
 GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC;
```

Almost every citation is `[1]`. But look at the assembly: chunks were ordered by score, and the prompt
lists them in that order â€” yet the *generator* is citing index 1 far more than chance would predict.

**Root cause.** Two problems stacked.
1. **Ordering**: chunks were inserted best-last (closest to the question), so `[1]` was the *weakest*
   chunk while the strongest was `[5]`. The model over-weighted the start of the context and cited it.
2. **Chunk truncation**: `perChunkCap` truncated chunks mid-table, so the source the model saw did not
   contain the row it cited.

**Fix.**
- Order highest-relevance-first for Q&A, and log the mapping from label â†’ chunk id so you can verify
  independently of the generator's citation.
- Raise `perChunkCap`; never truncate below a complete sentence or row.
- Add the deterministic output check from 13.6.5: citations must resolve, and numbers must appear in the
  cited source. That alone would have blocked all 11%.

```ts
const v = validateOutput(raw, { sources: assembledSources, policy: { requireCitations: true } });
if (!v.allow) return { ok: false, code: v.code, detail: v.detail };
```

**Lesson.** Citation correctness is verifiable without a judge. Make it a blocking check, not a nice
to-have.

---

## Scenario 5 â€” The agent loops forever on one failing tool

ðŸ”´ Advanced Â· **Must-know**

**Symptom.** A support agent burns its full token budget (~$3) on about 2% of conversations, always the
same shape: 24 tool calls, all `get_order`, then `max_steps`.

**Diagnosis.** Read a trace.

```ts
const trace = await loadTrace(runId);
const calls = trace.steps.flatMap((s) => s.toolCalls);
console.log(calls.length, [...new Set(calls.map((c) => c.name))]);
console.log(calls.slice(0, 6).map((c) => c.args));
```

Every call is `get_order({orderId: "ORD-9999"})`. That order does not exist. The tool returns:

```json
{"ok": false, "error": {"code": "not_found", "message": "order not found"}}
```

The model reads that, and calls the same tool with the same id.

**Root cause.** The error result did not tell the model what to do next, and nothing stopped repetition.
The loop had a step cap (which is why it terminated) but no loop detection and no *remedy* in the error.

**Fix â€” three layers.**

1. **Make the error actionable and terminal for that argument.** Errors should carry a `retryable: false`
   and a `remedy` hint:

```ts
if (!order) {
  return toolResult(false, null, {
    code: "not_found",
    message: "No order ORD-9999 exists for this account.",
    retryable: false,
    remedy: "Do not retry this order id. Either call search_orders to find the correct id, or ask the user which order they mean.",
  });
}
```

2. **Detect repetition in the loop and fail with a useful error**, so the user gets a sentence rather
   than a timeout:

```ts
const fingerprint = calls.map((c) => `${c.name}:${canonical(c.args)}`).sort().join("|");
if (fingerprints.includes(fingerprint)) {
  return { stop: "no_progress", userMessage:
    "I got stuck trying to look up that order. Could you give me the order number, or should I search your recent orders?" };
}
```

Also track per-tool failure counts and stop after 2 consecutive failures of the same tool.

3. **Bound the damage**: a per-tool call cap (`get_order: 4`) inside the overall budget.

```ts
const perTool = new Map();
for (const c of res.toolCalls) {
  const n = (perTool.get(c.name) ?? 0) + 1;
  perTool.set(c.name, n);
  if (n > TOOL_LIMITS[c.name]) return { stop: "tool_limit", tool: c.name };
}
```

**Lesson.** Loop detection is not a safety net, it is a UX feature. The real fix is making tool errors
instructive: an error is a message to the model, so write it as one.

---

## Scenario 6 â€” One tenant sees another tenant's data

âš« Expert

**Symptom.** A customer reports that a document search returned a chunk from a different company. Rare
(3 reports in a week), always in the "compare my invoices to last quarter's" flow.

**Diagnosis.** Reproduce with the tenant-switching code path.

```ts
const caller = { userId: "u1", tenantId: "acme", scopes: new Set(["docs:read"]) };
const input = { query: "invoices", topK: 5 };
const hits = await retrieve(input.query, { topK: input.topK });   // <-- no tenant filter!
```

Confirmed: one retrieval helper takes only a query and searches the whole corpus. Two other helpers do
filter by tenant.

**Root cause.** A missing tenant filter in one code path â€” and a red-team case that only tested the tool
layer, not retrieval. The prompt also *contained* the other tenant's content, so even with per-call
tool authorization the model had already been shown it.

**Fix â€” three layers.**

1. **Make unfiltered retrieval impossible by construction.** Tenant scoping is not an argument; it comes
   from a request-scoped context:

```ts
class RequestContext {
  constructor(readonly caller: CallerIdentity) {}
  // tenantId is not a parameter, so it cannot be forgotten.
  async searchCorpus(qv: Float32Array, k: number) {
    return db.query(
      `SELECT id, content FROM chunks
        WHERE tenant_id = $1 AND deleted_at IS NULL
        ORDER BY embedding <=> $2::vector LIMIT $3`, [this.caller.tenantId, toPgVector(qv), k]);
  }
}
```

2. **Post-hoc filter on retrieved content.** Defence in depth, because SQL filters get refactored away:

```ts
const hits = results.filter((h) => h.tenant_id === caller.tenantId);
if (hits.length < results.length) audit.append({ event: "cross_tenant_candidate_dropped", count: results.length - hits.length });
```

3. **An output guardrail for identifiers.** Every invoice/customer/document id in the answer must exist
   in the caller's data. This catches the case where the model somehow knows an id it should not.

```ts
const leaked = extractIdentifiers(answer).filter((id) => !knownIdsFor(caller).has(id));
if (leaked.length) return { ok: false, code: "unknown_identifier", detail: leaked };
```

4. **A red-team case** in CI: cross-tenant retrieval via query phrasing, not via tool arguments.

**Lesson.** Tenant isolation must be structural â€” a capability the code cannot express, rather than a
parameter a code path can forget. Any function that reads data should get identity from a scope, not
arguments.

## Scenario 7 â€” The eval score improved and production got worse

ðŸ”´ Advanced Â· **Must-know**

**Symptom.** A prompt change lifted the offline score from 0.71 to 0.79 on a 200-case golden set.
Two weeks later, escalation rate doubled and users complain the answers are longer but less useful.

**Diagnosis.** Line up the timeline and compare slices.

```ts
const cand = await runEval("support.v4");
const base = baselines.get("support.v3");
console.log("overall", base.overall, "â†’", cand.overall);
console.table(slices(base).map((s) => ({ slice: s.slice, base: s.acc, cand: sliceOf(cand, s.slice).acc, n: s.n })));
```

Overall improved. But per slice:

| slice | base | cand | n |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| short_factual | 0.95 | 0.96 | 60 |
| multi_tenant | 0.61 | 0.66 | 8 |
| long_context | 0.52 | 0.79 | 4 |

The entire improvement comes from `long_context`, which is 4 cases out of 200. That slice gained 0.27
Ã— 4 = 1.1 "case points" out of 200 Ã— ~0.1 = 20 aggregate points gained. **More than half the reported
improvement is four cases.**

Then check production:

```sql
SELECT recipe_id, count(*), round(avg(edit_distance_ratio),3) edits,
       round(avg(accept)::numeric,3) accept, round(avg(escalated)::numeric,3) escalate,
       round(avg(output_tokens)) out_tok
  FROM interaction_events
 WHERE feature='support.reply' AND at > now() - interval '30 days'
 GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1;
```

`support.v4` has higher acceptance but 40% higher output tokens and much higher edit distance. Users
accepted and then rewrote it. The eval's rubric rewarded "thoroughness"; users wanted brevity.

**Root cause.** Three compounding issues: (a) the eval set is unrepresentative â€” 4 long-context cases
dominating a headline metric; (b) the rubric had a "completeness" dimension that rewarded length and was
never calibrated against human preference; (c) the eval set contains no cases drawn from the segments
that escalated.

**Fix.**
1. **Report weighted-and-per-slice, never the aggregate alone.** Make the CI gate evaluate per slice with
   a minimum *n*, and refuse to promote on a slice with n < 20 without a human sign-off.
2. **Recalibrate the rubric against real human edits.** Take 200 accepted-then-edited answers, compute
   edit distance, and score them with the judge. Where edit distance is high, the judge should have
   scored low. It did not, so the rubric is wrong.
3. **Sample production clusters weekly** and diff against the eval distribution:

```ts
const prodClusters = await clusterProductionQueries(7);
const coverage = reportCoverage(prodClusters, CASES);
console.log(coverage.uncoveredClusters);   // e.g. "refund_for_partial_year: 3.1% of traffic, 0 cases"
```

4. **Add guardrail metrics to the gate**: output tokens, edit distance proxy, escalation â€” so a quality
   gain that doubles length is visible at promotion time.

**Lesson.** An offline score is a hypothesis about production, not a measurement of it. The two failure
modes to fear are an unrepresentative dataset and an uncalibrated judge, and per-slice reporting is the
cheapest defence against both.

## Scenario 8 â€” `context_length_exceeded` after the history feature launched

ðŸŸ¡ Intermediate Â· **Must-know**

**Symptom.** New failures, all on conversations over ~30 turns: the provider rejects the request outright.

**Diagnosis.**

```sql
SELECT count(*), round(avg(input_tokens)) avg_in, max(input_tokens) max_in,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE error_code = 'context_length_exceeded') errs
  FROM message_observations WHERE feature='chat' AND created_at > now() - interval '1 day';
```

`max_in` is above the model's context window. The window for this model is 200k, so `max_in` around
201k means the last turn pushed it over â€” the *next* request would too, but it fails first.

**Root cause.** History is projected with `maxChars` (13.2.8) but the budget was expressed in
*characters*, while the limit is in *tokens*. For conversations containing code or non-Latin text,
characters-per-token is well above 4. A 900k-character budget is ~250k tokens.

**Root cause (second).** No headroom was reserved for the output. `budget = window - maxOutputTokens`
was computed with `maxOutputTokens = 8000`, but long-form answers sometimes need more, and the provider
checks input + requested output against the window.

**Fix.**

```ts
// 1. Measure with the tokenizer, not characters.
const budgetTokens = tokenizer.encode(serialize(projected.messages)).length;

// 2. Reserve output plus a real margin.
const usable = windowTokens - req.maxOutputTokens - SAFETY_MARGIN_TOKENS;   // margin ~2k

// 3. Enforce it at send time, not at projection time.
if (budgetTokens > usable) {
  // Deterministic, not a model call: compact, then re-measure.
  await maybeCompact(store, conversationId, { windowTokens: usable, triggerFraction: 0.8, keepRecentTurns: 8, maxSummaryTokens: 600 });
  const reprojected = projectHistory(await store.history(conversationId), await store.summary(conversationId), budget);
  if (tokenCount(reprojected.messages) > usable) throw new ContextBudgetExceeded({ needed: tokenCount(reprojected.messages), usable });
}
```

Also: **fail gracefully.** Catch `context_length_exceeded` specifically and compact-and-retry *once*,
rather than surfacing a 500.

```ts
catch (e) {
  if (e.code === "context_length_exceeded") {
    await forceCompact(conversationId, { aggressive: true });
    return await attempt(1);          // one retry, deliberately
  }
  throw e;
}
```

**Lesson.** Token limits are token limits. Character-based budgeting is a bug waiting for a user with a
code-heavy conversation, and you must reserve output headroom or you will fail on the request *after*
the one that filled the window.

## Scenario 9 â€” A prompt edit broke nothing detectable and cost 15%

ðŸ”´ Advanced Â· **Must-know**

**Symptom.** Prompt `classify.v6` shipped. All evals passed with a comfortable margin (0.88 â†’ 0.86,
threshold 0.05). Two weeks later someone notices non-English inputs are much worse. Nobody noticed at
launch because the eval set is 100% English.

**Diagnosis.** Slice the golden set by language â€” there is only one slice:

```ts
console.log([...new Set(CASES.map((c) => c.metadata.slice))]);
// [ 'billing', 'account', 'incident', 'adversarial' ]
```

No `non_english` slice exists, so a total collapse there is invisible to the aggregate.

Re-run manually on a quick Spanish and German set:

```ts
const probe = ["necesito un reembolso", "ich kann mich nicht anmelden", "no puedo iniciar sesiÃ³n"];
for (const t of probe) {
  const r = await runOnce("classify.v6", t);
  console.log(t, "â†’", r.out);
}
```

The v6 prompt removed a line that said "respond in the language of the input." The model now emits the
canonical label with a translated reason field, or worse, mis-labels.

**Root cause.** Not a regression by the gate's definition â€” the gate measured what the dataset contains.
The real root cause is **eval coverage**: the dataset has no coverage of a dimension the product supports.

**Fix.**
1. **Extend the dataset** to cover languages the product claims to support, weighted by traffic.
2. **Make coverage a checked property, not a hope.** Tag every case with dimensions and assert coverage in
   CI:

```ts
export function assertCoverage(required: { slice: string; minCases: number }[]) {
  for (const { slice, minCases } of required) {
    const n = CASES.filter((c) => c.metadata.slice === slice).length;
    if (n < minCases) throw new Error(`eval coverage gap: ${slice} has ${n}/${minCases} cases`);
  }
}
```

3. **Compare the prompt diff against the removed lines.** A diff of `v5 â†’ v6` shows the deletion; that
   is a two-minute review that would have caught this. Add a prompt-diff reviewer checklist item: "list
   every capability or language removed."
4. **Sample production traffic by language** and add cases when a cluster is uncovered:

```ts
const byLang = await db.query(
  `SELECT language_hint, count(*) FROM interaction_events
    WHERE feature='classify' AND at > now() - interval '14 days' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC`);
```

**Lesson.** A gate can only catch what the dataset measures. Coverage gaps are silent, permanent, and
invisible in aggregates. Treat "what does my eval set *not* cover?" as a first-class review question.

## Scenario 10 â€” Streaming responses occasionally arrive out of order

ðŸ”´ Advanced Â· **Must-know**

**Symptom.** In a chat UI, some answers have the first and last sentences in the wrong order, or a
paragraph repeats. Only under load. Never in staging.

**Diagnosis.** Log the sequence numbers the server sends and the order the client applies them.

```ts
// server
let seq = 0;
for await (const ev of providerStream) {
  send("delta", { seq: seq++, text: ev.text, turnId });
}
// client
const seen = new Map();
for await (const ev of stream()) {
  if (ev.type === "delta") {
    if (seen.has(ev.data.seq)) continue;         // duplicate
    seen.set(ev.data.seq, ev.data.text);
    bubble.textContent = [...seen.keys()].sort((a,b)=>a-b).map(k=>seen.get(k)).join("");
  }
}
```

With the sequence map applied, the display is correct â€” confirming the bug is **duplicate frames**,
not reordering.

Where do duplicates come from? A proxy with automatic retry on a stalled upstream replays the buffered
prefix. Or: the app is deployed with two instances behind a load balancer, and a client reconnect
(retry) re-attaches mid-stream to a second instance.

**Root cause.** The SSE response is being retried by an intermediary. SSE is a long-lived response, and
anything that buffers-and-retries will replay. The app also has no `turnId`, so a reconnect cannot tell a
resumed stream from a new one.

**Fix.**
1. **Disable proxy retries/buffering for the SSE route** (`proxy_next_upstream off` for that location,
   `proxy_buffering off`).
2. **Add a `turnId` and `seq` to every frame**, and make the client idempotent per `seq` â€” which is
   correct regardless of who is duplicating.
3. **Make reconnects explicit.** A client that reconnects sends `Last-Event-ID`; the server resumes from
   a stored cursor, or restarts the turn cleanly with a new `turnId` and a `reset` frame the client acts
   on.

```ts
// client: on reconnect
if (ev.type === "reset") { seen.clear(); bubble.textContent = ""; }
// turn ids are scoped so a stale stream from a previous turn can never append to the current bubble
if (ev.data.turnId !== currentTurnId) continue;
```

**Lesson.** Assume anything between you and the browser will duplicate, reorder, and buffer. Design the
frame protocol to be idempotent, and treat the transport as untrusted. This is the same lesson as
13.2.6's idempotency, applied to a stream.

---

## Scenario 11 â€” The safety classifier is blocking legitimate security questions

ðŸŸ¡ Intermediate Â· **Must-know**

**Symptom.** Support ticket volume from the security team spiked with "assistant unavailable" messages.
Users asking things like "how do I rotate an API key" and "show me the auth logs for tenant X" are being
blocked.

**Diagnosis.** Inspect the blocks by category and by user segment.

```sql
SELECT segment, category, count(*) blocks, count(*) FILTER (WHERE appealed) appeals
  FROM guardrail_blocks WHERE at > now() - interval '7 days' GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY 3 DESC;
```

100% of blocks are in one segment (internal security engineers) and one category (`injection_pattern`).
Appeals are 0 â€” nobody appealed, they just gave up and used the terminal.

The specific rule firing is `/you\s+are\s+now\s+/i` plus a keyword heuristic on "auth logs". A legitimate
question â€” "you are now asking me to prove I own the account, what do you need?" â€” trips it.

**Root cause.** Two design mistakes. (a) A keyword heuristic on security vocabulary, which is exactly the
vocabulary a legitimate security team uses. (b) No appeal path, so false positives are invisible: they
look like product breakage, not like a guardrail problem.

**Fix.**

1. **Scope rules by trust and by segment.** The injection heuristic should be strongest on public,
   untrusted input and relaxed for an internal, authenticated, already-authorized segment â€” while still
   structurally enforced (least privilege) regardless.

```ts
const POLICY = {
  public:      { injection: "block", secretPatterns: "block" },
  partner:     { injection: "quote", secretPatterns: "allow" },
  internal:    { injection: "quote", secretPatterns: "allow" },
};
// Structural controls â€” least privilege, tenant scoping, egress restrictions â€” are unchanged for all.
```

2. **Replace the keyword heuristic with the structural control it was standing in for.** The reason we
   blocked "show me auth logs" was fear of unauthorized data access. That is an *authorization* problem;
   solve it by checking the caller's scopes, not by pattern-matching their vocabulary.

```ts
if (needsTenantData(args, caller)) {
  const missing = requiredScopes(args).filter((s) => !caller.scopes.has(s));
  if (missing.length) return deny("missing_scope", missing);
}
```

3. **Add an appeal path** and measure false-positive rate from it:

```ts
await notifications.enqueue({ type: "guardrail_appeal", userId: caller.userId, blockId, reason });
```

Track `block_rate` **by segment** and alert on divergence between segments â€” that divergence is your
false-positive detector.

4. **Never remove the structural controls.** Relaxing *prompt-level* heuristics under pressure is
   acceptable; relaxing tenant scoping or least privilege is not.

**Lesson.** Guardrails need a measured false-positive rate and an escape hatch that is itself audited.
A guardrail that silently blocks a whole customer segment is an outage you caused deliberately, and
because no one appeals, your dashboards will never tell you.

---

## Scenario 12 â€” The "smart" reranker made retrieval worse

ðŸ”´ Advanced Â· **Must-know**

**Symptom.** After switching rerankers (a smaller, faster, domain-fine-tuned-on-other-data model), recall@5
on the labelled set went *down* from 0.86 to 0.79, but p95 latency improved by 180ms. Someone shipped it
anyway because the latency win looked good in a dashboard.

**Diagnosis.** Compare per-query, not per-aggregate.

```ts
const base = baselines.get("rerank.a");
const cand = await evalRetrieval("rerank.b");
const moved = cand.perQuery.map((q, i) => ({
  query: q.query, before: base.perQuery[i].rr, after: q.rr, delta: q.rr - base.perQuery[i].rr,
})).filter((m) => Math.abs(m.delta) > 0.2);
console.table(moved.slice(0, 12));
```

A pattern emerges: every regression has a long chunk (>400 tokens) or contains a table. The new reranker
has a shorter effective input window and was trained on short passages.

**Root cause.** The reranker's `maxTokensPerPair` is 512 and it is silently truncating long candidates.
With short candidates it wins (hence better on the cases where it did not regress), so the aggregate on a
randomly-worded eval looked acceptable before the last gate was bypassed.

There is also a process failure: **the latency gate had no corresponding quality floor**, and someone had
authority to override the quality gate. Both are structural problems.

**Fix.**

1. **Fix the truncation.** Give the reranker complete candidates:

```ts
const candidates = fused.slice(0, 100);
const pairs = candidates.map((c) => ({
  id: c.id,
  // No silent truncation: over-length candidates are dropped and logged, not cut in half.
  tokens: tokenizer.encode(c.meta.text).length,
  text: c.meta.text,
})).filter((p) => p.tokens <= reranker.maxTokensPerPair);
const dropped = candidates.length - pairs.length;
if (dropped > 0) metrics.count("rerank_dropped_overlength", { n: dropped });
```

2. **Add a per-query regression gate**, not just an aggregate one:

```ts
const regressions = cand.perQuery
  .map((q, i) => ({ query: q.query, before: base.perQuery[i].rr, after: q.rr }))
  .filter((m) => m.before - m.after > 0.2);
if (regressions.length > 4) { console.error("gate FAIL: 5+ queries regressed materially"); process.exit(1); }
```

3. **Make latency improvements conditional on quality.** The gate should express "latency may improve
   **up to** X, quality may not regress at all":

```ts
if (qualityRegressed || latencyGain > maxAllowedLatencyGainForThisQualityDrop) fail();
```

4. **Characterise a reranker before adopting it** â€” token limits, effective context, training
   distribution â€” and record that in the config next to the model id.

**Lesson.** Every model in the pipeline has its own input limits and its own distribution. "Smaller and
faster" is a hypothesis; measure per query, watch for silent truncation, and never allow a latency gain
to be purchased with unmeasured quality loss.
